articleTitle: A Linear Microstrip Phased Array with Novel Integrated Phase Shifters
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The presented work explores the integration and excitation of a 1×4 microstrip linear phased antenna array in the ISM frequency band (2–3) GHz with recently introduced Magneto Static Responsive Structures (MRSs) phase shifters for beam steering applications. The integration process involves embedding MRS structures using two substrates to accommodate larger number of MRS cavities, thus enabling a wider range of achievable phases. The performance of the array is investigated for main beam steering angles of 0, 10, 20, and ±40 degrees. Initially, the corporate feed network is loaded with MRS structures, without the inclusion of the antennas, to ensure that the desired phases are achieved. Subsequently, patch antennas are integrated into the corporate feed network with embedded MRSs for full wave simulation. The results obtained from the full wave simulation of the phased array are then compared with those of directly excited array. Particularly, the peak gain was investigated for all configurations for the scanning angles of 0, 10,20 and ±40 degrees. The difference in gain was found 0.37 dB, 2.02 dB, 1.66 dB and 0.908 dB respectively between MRS-phase shifters excited and directly excited phased arrays. The close agreement of the radiation patterns between MRS phase shifters exited array with the directly excited array provides the potential of MRS phase shifters in enhancing the performance and functionality of integrated phased arrays. This finding establishes the viability of using MRS phase shifters in various applications, particularly in radar and satellite systems, where the improved gain and directivity characteristics of phased arrays can offer significant benefits.

articleTitle: From Images to Insights: Leveraging Machine Learning for Detecting and Classifying Alzheimer's
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The neurological condition marked by memory loss and increasing cognitive deterioration referred to as Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause in cognitive decline and deaths worldwide. Early and accurate detection of AD is crucial in providing timely interventions and improving patient outcomes. The objective of the present study was to leverage statistical and deep learning techniques to enhance magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) based detection and classification accuracy and reliability of AD. Our aim was to make accurate and timely predictions, that we achieved by using visual geometry group (VGG19) a deep learning approach used for classification tasks. The data used in this study was unbalanced across all four groups namely very mild demented, mild demented and moderate demented so, to assure reliable model training and evaluation data balancing techniques were employed to overcome biasness in the models. Experimental results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately detecting and classifying patients with high precision surpassing the legacy benchmark models by VGG19 at 88%.

articleTitle: Robust Stability Analysis of a Class of LTV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Many physical systems are inherently time-varying in nature. When these systems are linearized around a trajectory, generally, the resulting system is Linear Time-Varying (LTV). LTV systems describe an important class of linear systems and can be thought of as a natural extension of LTI systems. However, it is well known that, unlike LTI systems, the eigenvalues of an LTV system do not determine its stability. In this paper, the stability conditions for a class of LTV systems are derived. This class is composed of piecewise LTV systems, i.e. LTV systems that are piecewise linear in time. Sufficient conditions of stability are derived in the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) by using the Lyapunov stability criterion. The feasibility of LMIs guarantees the stability of a given piecewise LTV system. Furthermore, uncertain piecewise LTV systems with scalar parametric uncertainty are also considered. Sufficient conditions for robust stability of this case are also presented, which come out to be quasi-LMIs, which can be optimized using a bisection algorithm to find the bounds of uncertainty for which the system is stable. The proposed method is applied to the problem of pitch angle control of a space launch vehicle, and the results are presented.

articleTitle: SPVD: A Stroke Patient Motor Movements Video Dataset for AI Augmented Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce SPVD an RGB video dataset of stroke survivors' upper-limb and lower-limb motor movements in accordance with the National Institute of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) America. This dataset was collected as a milestone of our experiment, in the process of building an autonomous therapy system for the rehabilitation of stroke patients. The data inputs are camera videos and human skeleton joints captured throughout the motor movement exercises. The dataset has 10 action classes, over 100 video clips, and approx-imately 8.3 hours of video data, at a rate of 30 frames per second. The SPVD dataset consists of NIHSS-uploaded videos and videos of stroke survivors and healthy volunteers that were recorded with variations in camera orientation, recording positions, photometric effects, and cluttered backgrounds. It was further improvised by using data augmentation techniques for videos to overcome the limitations of available original videos. The dataset is available in a configuration of spatiotemporal features recordings, which includes angles and positions of human body joints. The intention in the creation of this dataset is to evaluate the patients performance using an autonomous system while validating the movement patterns during the execution of suggested rehabilitation exercises by NIHSS.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Power of Genes: Prediction of Breast Cancer Survival Assisted by Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The breast cancer prognosis plays a vital role in treatment planning and patient management. This study aims to investigate breast cancer prognosis using the molecular taxonomy of the breast cancer international consortium's (METABRIC) dataset for gene expression profiles. The considered dataset contains clinical and genomic data, providing a comprehensive prognostic assessment resource. Our study focuses on developing a predictive model using machine learning techniques. We pre-process the dataset using adaptive synthetic sampling (ADASYN), MinMax scaling, and feature reduction techniques. We assess the model's performance using accuracy, confusion matrix, and classification report metrics. We compare the performance of Logistic Regression and Random Forest classification techniques to determine efficacy in breast cancer prognosis. The results demonstrate the potential of gene expression profiles in accurately predicting breast cancer prognosis. The results show that the Logistic Regression achieves a certain level of performance while the Random Forest exhibits improved predictive capabilities.

articleTitle: Effect of Perovskite Thickness, Defect Density and Temperature on a CH3NH3SnI3 based Perovskite Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Solar energy has emerged as a very effective renewable source of generating electricity that also reduces carbon emission and global warming. Conventional solar panels comprise of silicon wafers and are vastly used on commercial basis. Despite abundance and domination of silicon in solar cell manufacturing industry, it does have some drawbacks. Silicon is an indirect band gap semiconductor having large energy difference between direct band gap (3.5eV) and indirect band gap (1.1eV). For this reason, Silicon has low absorption and thus has an impact on the efficiency of solar cell. For better absorption, the thickness is required to be increased, which itself is not a very favorable approach as it increases manufacturing cost and complexity. Recently, Perovskite materials have proven to be very effective alternate, as they are much better in absorbing sunlight and are also crystallised as thin film, as compared to silicon layer. The low cost and high efficiency of Perovskite Solar cells has attracted interest of the world. In the mix of technologies for alternate energy, organic/inorganic halide perovskite solar cells have been declared the game changer and in a very short time span, claimed efficiencies >20%. This remarkable progress further highlights the possibility for realizing the potential even deeper. For achieving better efficiency, preventing electron-hole recombination can also be a practical approach for which Hole transport material (HTM) and Electron Transport Material (ETM) are used. This is because Hole Transport Layer (HTL) have energy levels that attract holes from absorber layer and act as barrier for electrons, and similarly Electron Transport Layer (ETL) have energy levels that attract electrons from absorber layer and act as barrier for holes, thus prevents recombination. In this paper, SCAPS 1D simulator is utilized to implement a Solar cell design (FTO/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/CuI/Au) with Optimized parameters, for which the simulation results demonstrated Voc̭1.0565 V, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>̭32.15 mA/cm2, FF= 80.43% and PCE= 27.33%. We also analyzed the effect of perovskite layer thickness, defect density, interface defect density and temperature on the performance of proposed design. The optimized design can not only be useful for development of a cost effective yet efficient solar cell, it can also surely contribute in future advancements and development of advanced Perovskite solar cells.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Pakistani Sign Language Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: More than 250,000 hearing impaired Pakistanis communicate using Pakistani Sign Language (PSL) in everyday life. An automated system for PSL recognition will be of benefit to this hard of hearing community. This study proposes a recognition system for PSL employing Deep Learning techniques. The system has been trained and tested on 36 static and 3 dynamic gestures of the PSL alphabet. The dataset consists of 5120 images and 353 videos from 10 native PSL signers. A Convolutional Neural Network and a Long-term Recurrent Convolutional Network architecture has been developed for static and dynamic gestures recognition respectively. The models have achieved classification accuracies of 96.1% and 98.6%.

articleTitle: Beam Steering of a Circularly Polarized X/Ku-band Shared Aperture Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents 4-port patch array antenna designed for dual-frequency operation at X-band (12.17 GHz) and Ku-band (17.5 GHz) with shared aperture arrangement. The 4-port antenna demonstrates beam steering capabilities of ±20°, while maintaining a side lobe level below -10 dB and a gain of 10 dB. Single port unit cell exhibits a gain of 7 dB, while the 2 x 2 and 4 x 4 array attain 12 dB and 18 dB gain, respectively. All antenna configurations are designed using Arlon Diclad 880 with ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of 2.2 and thickness = 0.76 mm. The radiation efficiency achieved is 90% and the axial ratio stays below 3 dB, thus confirming the circularly polarization. Its high gain, excellent radiation efficiency, and low side lobe level make it well-suited for many RF applications.

articleTitle: Admission, Association, and Rate Maximization in a UAV Assisted User Clustering Based Downlink Hybrid Multiple Access HetNets
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper addresses the future requirements of extensive coverage, high data rate, and support for highly interactive multimedia applications by exploring the benefits of fifth-generation (5G) networks. Existing studies have separately investigated unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), heterogeneous networks (HetNets), orthogonal multiple access (OMA), non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), and user clustering. However, the collective impact of these factors has not been explored together. HetNet is a collection of base stations (BSs) as macro BS (MBS) and small BS (SBS). A comprehensive approach by combining these elements, i.e., UAV-assisted user clustering based downlink hybrid-multiple access (hybrid-MA) in HetNet, is proposed to maximize sum rates, taking into account factors such as user admission in clusters, user association with BSs, power allocation, the distance of users from BSs, and minimum rate requirements. A novel network model is presented and the problem is formulated as mixed integer nonlinear programming (MINLP), which is solved using an outer approximation algorithm (OAA). Comparative evaluations with existing strategies, i.e., OMA-MBS-only, NOMA-MBS-only, hybrid-MA-MBS only, and hybrid-MA-HetNet, demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed technique in terms of user admission, user association, and sum rate.

articleTitle: ISLAP: Advancing RFID System Security through an Improved Succinct and Lightweight Authentication Protocol
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A radio frequency identification (RFID) system employs radio waves to communicate a unique pattern between a tag implanted in an RFID card and a reader to validate a user's identity and provide access. Because of its simplicity, it is regarded as a preferred authentication method. Along with extensive implementation, RFID's rapid growth raises several security challenges and threats. As a result, a secure authentication mechanism is required to address RFID security concerns. Among the different security techniques created by researchers, Succinct and Lightweight Authentication Protocol (SLAP) is a low-effort RFID architecture that can withstand security threats. According to our findings, previously published approaches are subject to stolen authenticator assaults, impersonation attacks, and anonymity issues. This research proposes an improved and efficient solution for RFID devices based on a lightweight authentication protocol known as ISLAP. This addresses the security issues and attacks observed in prior techniques. The proposed protocol is evaluated and validated using ProVerif, a software program designed to do reasoning about a protocol's security features. The proposed protocol was sufficiently safe, with optimal output compared to alternative solutions.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Monitoring Using a Photo Detector-Based Approach: A Promising Alternative for Diabetes Management
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus usually known as diabetes has been an active issue for a long period. Monitoring of Blood glucose levels is one of the important physiological information for medical professionals. Non-invasive detection of blood glucose levels is necessary for monitoring and managing diabetes and reducing the need for frequent finger pricks as invasive methods. Non-invasive measurement of blood glucose provides a convenient and pain-free alternative to traditional invasive methods. The traditional methods require pricking of the finger for taking blood samples and calibration for proper results. Non-calibrated devices can lead to faulty results. In this study, a photo detector-based approach is used to measure the blood glucose level. The system is based on a photodetector sensor that detects the changes in light absorption caused by variations in blood glucose levels. In this study, we performed experiments on two sets of groups, one with normal and the other with fasting state to compare the invasive and non-invasive values of glucose in different subjects to make a standard non-invasive glucometer system. The evaluation was conducted on a group of participants before and after the ingestion of glucose during the procedure. The sensor was placed superficially on the fingertip to acquire the photoplethysmography signal along with the traditional measurement method for reference blood glucose values. The MATLAB-based algorithm has been designed to further filter and process the signal and measure the blood glucose level. The results indicate a strong correlation between photoplethysmography detector-based measurement and the reference blood glucose levels. The non-invasive method exhibited promising accuracy and reliability in estimating blood glucose concentrations. The proposed approach provides a non-invasive measurement of blood glucose level which improves the quality of life for individuals with diabetes.

articleTitle: Chemical Degradation of Jute Reinforced Biobased VE Composites and Recyclability of Jute Fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Natural fibers reinforced bio-based thermosets are green alternatives offering biobased solutions for climate change and depleting fossil fuels. Apart from sustainability, the researchers are looking for viable options to degrade and recycle natural fiber-reinforced biobased thermosets to reduce landfill and white pollution. This study embodies the novel approach of chemically degrading treated jute fiber-reinforced vanillin epoxy (VE) thermosets using an acid degradation technique coupled with the recyclability of jute fibers. The recycled jute fiber was re-impregnated with biobased vanillin epoxy resin using the VARTM technique. SEM and flexural properties of recycled jute fiber reinforced VE thermoset showed the potential for reusability of jute fiber. This study showed the prospective for recycling natural fiber from biobased thermoset matrixes reducing landfill and adding advantages of biobased materials.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniaturized Dual-Band Frequency Selective Surface for Wi-Fi Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, a compact frequency selective surface (FSS) with dual-band stop feature is introduced for shielding the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz Wi-Fi bands. The FSS comprised of metallic patches and meanders on both sides of the dielectric substrate. Moreover, the metallic patterns on both layers are connected through the vias. The designed structure has miniaturized unit size of 0.048 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> x 0.048 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free space wavelength at the lower resonating frequency of 2.4 GHz. The proposed structure is polarization independent due to the 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> rotational symmetry of elements on the top and bottom side of the substrate. The corresponding surface current and electric field distribution is illustrated to comprehend the resonance behavior of the structure. The compact unit cell, low thickness, angular stability for both the TE and TM polarization are the eminent attributes of the proposed design.

articleTitle: On the Time-Variant Step Size Posterior LMS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The conventional least mean square (LMS) algorithm can be regarded as a numerical approximation of a set of first-order ordinary differential equations developed using the explicit method. The convergence and performance characteristics of the LMS algorithm are determined by the relationship between the fixed gain and the input correlation statistics. The problem is less severe in the normalized LMS algorithm which removes the dependence on the input correlation statistics but limits the parameter value to a finite fixed interval for stable behavior. In this paper, we show, perhaps for the first time, the stability condition for the vector case of the LMS-type algorithm developed using the implicit method. Based on this, we present a time-variant step size LMS algorithm. Empirical studies demonstrate the superior convergence and steady-state behavior of the proposed filter.

articleTitle: A Sensitive Dual-Stage Active Wideband Electric Field Probe for Near-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A dual-stage, wideband, and active electric field probe is being introduced in this paper. Due to the rapid change in the electric and electronic field industry, Electromagnetic Compatibility EMC and the problem of Electromagnetic Interference EMI became a must for study, and to overcome the main source for the unwanted electrical effects. The probe design is divided into two stages, the first stage is the passive part of the probe, which is an ultrawideband probe that works from 10KHz to 20GHz. It is a PCB with four layers with high-performance dielectric (dielectric constant is 3.55 and 3.3). The second part is the active part, which is broadband and can enhance the probe sensitivity, which works from 10KHz to 500MHz. The two stages will be connected via a coaxial cable and SMA connector. The dual-stage probe can work with a wideband Data Acquisition System DAQ up to 500MHz with a gain of up to 41dB and a low NF. It is a two-layer PCB. The dual-stage probe can enhance the sensitivity by filtering and amplifying the signal to meet the DAQ system requirements. The first and second stages both can work separately, the passive probe can work from up to 20GHz and the second active part can work as a front-end PCB from up to 500MHz with 41dB gain.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of a Fuzzy Supervisory Controller for the Rotary Inverted Pendulum
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The control of Rotary Inverted Pendulum (RIP) is a fundamental but challenging issue in control system theory. RIP is a complicated and nonlinear electromechanical system. In this paper three controllers are designed. These controllers will drive the pendulum from its hanging-down position to upright position in a vertical plane and then hold it there. First, a detailed mathematical model has been developed by applying physics and electrical engineering principles. The first controller is a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller. The second one is a Fuzzy Logic controller in which triangular membership functions are used for fuzzification process. In this controller, Mamdani inference engine is also used to evaluate the rule-base. To ensure the optimum performance of PID controller, a third controller is introduced which is Fuzzy supervisory controller. In case of electrical and environmental disturbances or change in system parameters, this controller automatically tunes the conventional PID controller. The simulation results of PID, Fuzzy logic and Fuzzy supervisory controllers are compared. The effectiveness and robustness of Fuzzy supervisory controller is ensured by creating disturbance in the system manually. Finally, a tracking system is designed under the supervision of Fuzzy supervisory controller and its performance is observed by applying different time varying inputs.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Surface Rasorber Design Based on Miniaturized Elements to Obtain High Angle Stability
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A miniaturized frequency selective rasorber permitting transmission in specific band and absorption at other frequencies in vicinity of transmission is presented in this paper. The design integrates a miniaturized band pass FSS with a lossy layer. The air as transmission line of length 5 mm is used between the two layers. The electrical size of the structure is reduced through high meandered inductance and large capacitance produced between the gap of meandered lines. The two layered structure is miniaturized to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.036\lambda_{0}\times 0.036\lambda_{0} mm^{2}$</tex> dimensions. The wide band transmission centre frequency is designed at 2 GHz. The fractional band width of the pass band is 76%. The higher frequencies above the transmission band are absorbed. The 96% peak of maximum absorption rate is distributed at 3.9 GHz at transmission zero of the band pass FSS, where it behaves like a reflecting wall to the lossy layer. The rasorber surface is polarization symmetric and stable at oblique angles up to 60°. The proposed design with low profile characteristic can be applied in frequently used L and S band applications for RCS reduction and stealth objectives.

articleTitle: Neural Machine Translation System for Pakistani Languages
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Neural machine translation (NMT) is the most widely used machine translation framework for bilingual machine translation and it relies on parallel corpus which is not available for low resource languages which include majority of Pakistani languages. This research entails the creation of a large scale Pakistan Multilingual Corpus (PMC) with 19 million parallel sentences for Punjabi(Shahmukhi), Punjabi(Gurmukhi), Pashto, Sindhi, Urdu and English. This study uses NMT to create sophisticated bidirectional and multilingual NMT systems for Pakistani languages. We have built bidirectional Gurmukhi to Shahmukhi NMT models (gur<->shah), bilingual and an English-centric many-to-one NMT model for Pakistani languages including Punjabi Shahmukhi as there is no NMT model exists for Punjabi Shahmukhi. Comprehensive testing and evaluation process is done to gauge the system's efficacy and accuracy.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Nonlinear Control Techniques: Inverted Pendulum on a Cart
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: An in depth comparative study is conducted between nonlinear dynamic inversion based controller and immersion and invariance based controller. Immersion and Invariance (I&I) is a constructive nonlinear control design methodology for robust and adaptive controller designs. I&I method, as the name implies, mainly relies upon the notions of system immersion and manifold invariance. The basic idea is to design a control law that asymptotically immerses the system dynamics into the reducedorder desired dynamics. In this work, Immersion and Invariance based controller is systematically compared against nonlinear dynamic inversion based controller using a benchmark control problem of an inverted pendulum on cart (IPCS). Simple yet rich dynamics of an inverted pendulum on cart poses an interesting problem to control. Stabilization and control of IPCS has posed as a benchmark problem for many researchers to test out different control techniques. This motorized contraption consists of a vertical pendulum with a pivot point mounted on a cart. The cart is able to move horizontally through the application of a parallel force, which in turn is the input to the system. The IPCS is a case of an under actuated mechanical system, where the angular acceleration of the pendulum cannot be directly controlled. In this work, I&I based controller designed for IPCS, and its robustness properties are compared with nonlinear dynamic inversion control techniques.

articleTitle: SiC coated Hastelloy X via wet chemistry for Corrosion Protection in Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The iodine sulfur cycle, which is used for hydrogen production, requires materials that can withstand the corrosive properties of sulfuric acid at high temperatures. To address this, researchers explored the use of a silicon carbide (SiC) coating on Hastelloy X (HX) through a wet chemistry process. This coating method was considered a cost-effective alternative to physical vapor deposition (PVD) coatings. The researchers conducted immersion tests on the coated specimens and compared them with bare and PVD-coated samples in previous studies. The results showed that the SiC-coated HX exhibited the best corrosion resistance among the different samples when exposed to 98 wt% sulfuric acid at a temperature of 120°C. The presence of the SiC coating on the sample was confirmed using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and the morphology of the coated sample was examined using an optical microscope. The images obtained from the microscope analysis showed no changes in the sample's morphology after the corrosion testing. Further structural analysis of the coated samples revealed the presence of SiC-Si02 after annealing. The presence of silicon dioxide (SiO2) contributed to the improved corrosion resistance of the coated samnple.

articleTitle: Semantic Similarity of the Holy Quran Translations with Sentence-BERT
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research study investigates the use of Multilingual Large Language Models (MLLM) to determine multilingual semantic similarity between the Holy Quran and its various translations to identify translation closeness and the ability of LLMs in this area. We conducted an investigation focusing on the analysis of semantic contexts in the translations of the Holy Quran from the Indo-European language family. We specifically selected 16 multilingual translations to explore the translation semantics. To further explore the semantic similarities, we analyzed surah Fatiha (The opening chapter) and compared it with the multilingual translation. The primary objective of our study was to gain insights into the semantic inter-connected across different language families.

articleTitle: Design of a Planar Four-Port Microstrip Triplexer using Stub-Loaded Coupled Line Resonator for Advanced Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In the realm of high-frequency devices, effective management of circuit interactions holds the utmost significance within intricate environments. In light of this, a planar four-port microstrip triplexer employing a stub-loaded coupled line res-onator structure has been meticulously designed and examined. The triplexer filter exhibits seven transmission poles, strategically incorporated to ensure optimal performance across all three passbands. Targeting operation frequencies of 2.55 GHz, 3.94 GHz, and 5.74 GHz, the proposed triplexer is fabricated on a compact Rogers Duroid 5880 substrate. With insertion losses of 0.36 dB at 2.55 GHz, 0.53 dB at 3.94 GHz, and 0.33 dB at 5.75 GHz, the triplexer demonstrates excellent alignment between measured and simulated results, thereby substantiating its efficacy in meeting the specified requirements.

articleTitle: Multipath Mitigation Using Discrete Wavelet Denoising for GNSS Point Positioning
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Multipath error is difficult to resolve for any communication system. For positioning solutions through Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), multipath affects the positioning accuracy especially for dynamic applications. The main challenge in resolving multipath is its random nature implying it is difficult to create a generic multipath model. This paper proposes discrete wavelet denoising approach to mitigate the multipath error. The input GNSS code-minus-carrier (CMC) observations are smoothed using simple moving average filter. Discrete wavelet denoising is applied to the smoothed observations to filter the multipath in decomposition process and construct clean GNSS observations which are post processed for positioning. Two dynamic data sets tested for this technique, with results compared using dynamic time warping, show that wavelet denoised data generates higher precision positioning results.

articleTitle: A Short-Term Load Forecasting by Using Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Forecasting a region's energy needs, or “load,” involves calculating how much power will be required in the future. It often implies past data and considers various parameters such as weather, time of day, season, etc., that may affect energy consumption. Short-Term Load Forecasting (STFL) involves looking forward anywhere from twenty-four hours to a few weeks to estimate the power demand. It is mainly use for load balancing, unit commitment and economic dispatch operations. Therefore, in this paper, a novel approach consisting of Quantile Long Short-Term Memory (Q-LSTM) is presented for a short-term forecasting of the load data collected from the database of Electricity System Operator (ESO) for Great Britain. The validity of the suggested approach is confirmed by comparing the forecasted outcomes with those of well-established methods: LSTM and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with LSTM (CNN-LSTM) using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAPE). The findings express the superiority of the proposed system over LSTM and CNN-LSTM networks. Moreover, the RMSE and MAPE of Q-LSTM at quantile of 0.1 are 9.3% and 23.84% better than LSTM network, respectively. Similarly the recorded values of RMSE and MAPE of Q-LSTM at quantile of 0.1 are improved by 8.9% and 9.3%, respectively, as compared to CNN-LSTM network.

articleTitle: Cascaded Switching Power Amplifier for Imaging SONAR
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In sonar application, switching amplifiers can be used to drive the transducer. Considering the high efficiency, switching amplifiers are ideal for sonar transducer applications because they can deliver high power without generating excessive heat. A modular switching amplifier (SA) is presented that was built and designed to drive a specific acoustic transducer with 400 kHz resonance frequency. The cascaded configuration is intended to render the modularity feature, enabling the connection of two or more individual SA resulting in programmable power ratings, Isolation between inverters and transducers is ensured using a high-frequency transformer. The amplifier needs an impedance matching network (IMN) to efficiently transfer power from the source to the load and limit output total harmonic distortion (THD). Design of IMN ensures the required voltage gain of the amplifier, meet peak power demand of 500W from two low-voltage source of 48 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</inf>. The simulation and experimental findings demonstrate that the developed amplifier, when used in an inductive configuration, results in significantly lower power losses. The parallel RLC has set the amplifier's voltage gain to 2.55, producing 620 W peak output, a sinusoidal waveform at 400 kHz with 3.1 % THD.

articleTitle: Review of Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR), Polarimetric ISAR Imaging and Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this work, a brief but a complete review of Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) imaging theory is given and the usage of polarimetric imaging concepts in ISAR imaging is shared. First, a very quick summary of ISAR imaging concept is revisited to highlight the key parameters of ISAR imaging such as the geometry, the formulation and the resolution metrics. Then, an example of two-dimensional ISAR image is shared. In the second part of the paper, one of the most comprehensive research topics of ISAR imaging that is polarimetric ISAR is being covered. First, the aspects of polarimetric data collection are revisited. Then, Pauli decomposition technique and its usage in ISAR images are explained. Then, an example of polarimetric ISAR image is provided to together with the polarimetric interpretation of the resultant image.

articleTitle: Deformation Behavior of 3D Printed Auxetic Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Poisson's ratio is a mechanical property to count the lateral behavior of the material under axial loading. Auxetic structures show infrequent mechanical responses of negative Poisson's ratios, which are attributable to the entangled deformation features that characterize interconnected elements of macro structural formation. Because of their remarkable mechanical characteristics under bending, shear, and compression stresses, auxetic structures found a wide range of applications in the aerospace and automobile industries due to their negative Poisson ratio. Novel auxetic structures were fabricated by modifying pre-existing ones identified in the literature and evaluating their deformation behavior. Auxetic structures are manufactured by using poly-lactic acid materials using fused deposition modeling. The innovative structures' in-plane mechanical performance under uniaxial compression stresses was assessed experimentally. It was observed that the structure deformed and collapsed row-wise and the S1 has greater stress absorption with no buckling while the S2 involved buckling.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Antenna for WiFi/WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research paper presents a new design for a dual-band compact microstrip based patch antenna that covers 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and 5.8 GHz WiMAX applications by using the Defected Ground Structure (DGS) technique and three-quarter circles separated by slots as a patch. The antenna is designed using an FR-4 illumination with a dielectric permittivity of 4.7 and a height of 1.6 mm. The rectangular patch has dimensions of 42.7 mm in length and 47.7 mm in width. The performance of the antenna has been evaluated using CST, yielding the best results, such as a return loss of -23.85 dB, VSWR of 1.18, directivity of 2.49 dBi, and gain of 2.14 dBi, and a return loss of -21.37 dB, VSWR of 1.120, directivity of 4.76 dBi, and gain of 3.13 dB for the resonant frequencies of 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz respectively. Feeding network is also designed for real time applications. The antenna is fabricated and tested for validation, return loss of -12.364 dB at 2.4 GHz and -13.417 dB at 5.8 GHz was obtained. Therefore, the innovative designed antenna meets all the criteria for a next-generation electrically small antenna, simple, and easy to build.

articleTitle: On Dynamic Mode Decomposition: Application on Flow Past an Oscillatory Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The capacity of Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) as a data-inspired methodology to discern spatial-temporal structures and predict future states in intricate dynamical systems is the focal point of this investigation. This methodology is employed on a system comprising a flow past a cylinder at a Reynolds number of 250 and a Strouhal number of 2.5. The study aims at utilizing DMD to deconstruct the underpinning flow dynamics, detect coherent structures associated with spatial modes, and assess its predictive capacity. The investigation pivots around three unique scenarios, each highlighting a different boundary condition for the cylinder. These include the flow dynamics past a stationary cylinder, perpetually anti-clockwise rotating cylinder, and an oscillatory rotating cylinder, with the oscillation frequency equal to the vortex shedding frequency of the first case. The examination of these cases allows for an evaluation of DMD's prowess in capturing the modes relevant to each flow condition and its potential for future state prediction. The implementation of DMD allows for the effective detection of the dominant modes pertinent to the diverse flow conditions. This facilitates a comprehensive understanding of the spatiotemporal characteristics of the flow past the cylinder. The temporal analysis of modes in each case identifies the energy flow and capturing of dominant frequencies among different modes, indicating system harmonics. This phenomenon is specific to Hopf bifurcation, which is the characteristic of a periodic flows at Re > 47. Using the identified modes, the temporal evolution of the flow is extrapolated, enabling accurate predictions that extend beyond the available data. This aspect is especially significant in areas like flow control and optimization, where accurate future state prediction is vital.

articleTitle: Space-Time-Processing Optimization for Accurate DOA Estimation in Ultra Wideband DF System
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research paper presents a novel direction of arrival (DOA) estimation technique that fuses multiple processing techniques to enhance accuracy while mitigating cost and space constraints. In order to reduce the system cost owing to hardware, the number of antenna elements restricted to six. The antenna orientation especially designed in co-prime ratios of 2:5:3 to minimize ambiguity and to ensure that the DOA estimation is insensitive to the orientation of the platform, carrying the antennas. The proposed scheme fuses common angle search(CAS) technique, amplitude comparison and correlative interferometry with interpolation technique to address the limitations offered by each individual technique. The proposed scheme achieves nearly real-time DOA estimation with maximum RMSE around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1^{\circ}$</tex>, field of view <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40^{\circ}$</tex> and maximum antenna separation around 200mm.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Learning Model for the Detection of Phishing Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In recent years, phishing attacks have emerged as one of the most serious threats to web users, businesses, and internet service providers, particularly in remote working environments. Attackers use phishing emails and websites to steal confidential client information. Because of technological innovation and information flow, attackers can easily obtain target information and execute sophisticated phishing attacks accordingly. As a result, detecting phishing attempts is more important than ever. Machine learning (ML) approaches can detect phishing attempts. This study introduces a new ensemble technique for detecting online phishing attacks. It uses an ensemble method that employs ML classifiers such as Random Forest Classifier, Artificial Neural Network (ANN), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), SVM, XGB, Bagging, Logistic Regression, and Decision Tree. In detecting online phishing attacks, this ensemble technique exceeds previous studies. The proposed method detects phishing assaults with 96.2% accuracy.

articleTitle: Sparsity Adaptive RIS in MIMO Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), a novel and developing wireless communication technology, has drawn a lot of interest of researchers. RIS consists of a large number of antenna arrays that require high processing power. However, the signals involved in RIS are sparse in some domains. Compressive sensing (CS) could be an appropriate choice to deal with these limits. It can recover sparse or compressed signals with fewer measurements than conventional approaches. In traditional CS algorithms, the accuracy of the recovery signal depends on the sparsity level, as sparsity increases, more accurate signal is recovered. In previous research, structured sparsity was exploited to develop a compressive sensing channel recovery algorithm. In this contribution, novel sparsity adaptive RIS have been proposed. The sparsity level is increased by adjusting the size of RIS and transmitting antennas according to the number of users. The numerical results show that sparsity can be increased by varying the sizes of RIS. In this way, better performance in normalized mean square error (NMSE) can be obtained.

articleTitle: Coverage-Driven and Constrained-Randomized Sub-System Level Verification Methodology for RISC-V Based SoCs
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents the robust sub-system level verification framework for RISC- V based SoCs. The sub-system level verification ensures that the individual modules of a system under test are functioning correctly. The proposed framework adopts a hybrid model verification environment based on coverage driven verification (CDV) and constrained randomized verification (CRV) methodologies. Moreover, the universal verification methodology (UVM) is adopted to make testbench reusable and configurable. The SweRVolf, a RISC- V-based SoC with a dual-issue 9-stage SweRV-EH1 core, is used to prove the applicability of proposed sub-system verification environment. The sub-system design under verification (DUV) consists of AXI-to-WB bridge, Wishbone interconnect and GPIO interface. The proposed framework verifies each module first at IP level and then integrates all the universal verification components (UVCs) together to perform sub-system level verification. The CDV is used for coverage closure and covering all possible corner cases while the CRV is considered for exhaustive and complete verification of the D UV. 25 different random and directed tests have been applied to the sub-system DUV. For functional coverage 21 separate cover-groups are written. Each cover and cross cover-group targets specific feature of the DUV. The proposed hybrid verification model is able to achieve 100% toggle coverage both at IP and sub-system level. The proposed approach is best suited for applications focusing sub-system level designs using pre-verified IPs. The proposed verification framework could seamlessly be integrated with any RISC- V based SoCs testbench environment assuming that the same sub-system design topology is considered.

articleTitle: Fast Sparse Magnetic Resonance Image Reconstruction via a Dual Formulation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing trend in sparse modeling to reduce the scan time in magnetic resonance imaging while maintaining the diagnostic quality of the images. In this paper, we reformulate the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_{1}$</tex>-penalized regression problem with a total variation constraint for magnetic resonance image reconstruction via the Lagrange dual function and develop an efficient algorithm for the dual problem. Furthermore, we discuss model selection via an information criterion to find the optimal regularization parameters in the optimization problem. Empirical studies using spatial brain magnetic resonance images demonstrate that the algorithm exhibits superior convergence properties and achieves higher quality reconstruction in comparison to existing methods.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Characterization of Magnesium doped Zinc Sulphide Nanoparticles to Study Optical Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Pure Zinc Sulphide (ZnS) and Magnesium doped Zinc Sulphide (Mg:ZnS) nanoparticles having concentrations 1%, 3%, 5%, 7% and 9% were prepared by Chemical precipitation technique using zinc acetate, sodium sulphide and magnesium chloride. The impact of dopant concentrations on the band gap and optical characteristics of nanoparticles have been studied. The band gaps of the nanoparticles were calculated from the UV-visible absorption spectra. FTIR analysis was performed to identify organic and inorganic material in the nanoparticles formed. The Raman Spectroscopy was also done in order to observe the rotational, vibrational or other low-frequency modes in the system and to identify the shape of the crystal structure.

articleTitle: A Novel Continuous Variable Transmission for Underwater Towed Array Sonar Winching System
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Winching system for underwater Towed Array Sonar is very important as they provide numerous tactical advantages to the user. The winching system consists of a drum and a guiding system to guide the array in proper winding on the drum. Two types of designs are common. In the first design the drum and guiding system are driven by independent motors. This design provides more flexibility but is complex to implement. In the second design which is the most common because of its simplicity, the drum and guiding system are connected through a gearing system having a fix gear ratio and are driven by a single motor. Although systems with fix gear ratio are simple but they cannot adapt to minor variations generally found in diameter of the towed array. Moreover, they cannot be used for winding towed arrays in which the acoustic module has a larger diameter then the rest of the array. The present paper solves the aforementioned problems by proposing a novel Continuous Variable Transmission(Cvt)which can replace the fix gear ratio system with a variable gear ratio system. 3D Mod el of the new CVT along with geometrical analysis has been given. It is pertinent to mention that unlike the commercially available CVTs, the new CVT can achieve negative gear ratios without the use of clutches and epicyclic gears. Moreover, the new CVT has two traction points for better torque transmission. The new CVT in addition to solving the aforementioned problem, is also suitable for Vehicles and Robotics applications.

articleTitle: Nickel based Nanostructured Meta-absorber for Visible and Infrared Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Effective nanoscale light control results in many fascinating applications, such as thermal photovoltaics, imaging, energy harvesting, and others. All these applications require wide-bandwidth, compact size, angularly stable, and thermally robust absorbers, which is a significant challenge to be handled. Thus, this work demonstrates a simple and low-cost solution for realizing a wide-bandwidth nanostructured absorber. The engineered nanoscale absorber consists of a simple “H” shape nickel metal geometry, which has characteristics of wide bandwidth, polarization insensitivity, and overall miniaturization in absorber design. Absorber fabrication with Nickel conducting metal is also low-cost because Nickel meets all nanofabrication requirements with a high melting point of 1453 °C. The nickel-based absorber exhibits above 93% absorption in the complete wideband (400–2500 nm) optical spectrum. In addition, a comprehensive absorption profile analysis is also performed by changing the incident and polarization angles of the electromagnetic source. The investigated analysis of the nanostructures meta-absorber proved that the absorption profile remains above 82% over the whole wavelength spectrum of (400–2800 nm). Thus, attractive features such as simple geometry, wide bandwidth, polarization insensitivity, and angular and thermal robustness of the designed nanostructures meta-absorber make it a suitable choice for thermophotovoltaics, and solar energy harvesting, applications.

articleTitle: GaAs Based Ku-Band Low Noise Amplifier Design Using Simplified T-Matching Network and Current-Reuse Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) using simplified T-matching network and current-reuse topology for Ku-Band applications. A three stage LNA is designed and simulated using 0.25µm GaAs pHEMT process in Advanced Design System (ADS) software. The proposed LNA design operates in 13.5-18.5 GHz frequency range and exhibits excellent performance, featuring <2.1 dB noise figure, 24.5~26.5 dB gain, 12.1 dBm OP1dB and it is matched to 50 Ω at input and output ports. The presented self-biased LNA architecture requires a single supply voltage of 5 V and draws 93.7 mA current. Due to its compact size, it is ideal for hybrid and MCM assemblies. The overall size of the chip is 1.7mm x1.1mm.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Empowered Dispersion Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Metasurface-enabled optical holography can effectively provide nanometer-scale resolution due to the unprecedented ability of the metasurfaces to engineer the electromagnetic wave properties (amplitude, polarization, and phase). This has led to the evolution of the new era of numerous advanced applications in virtual reality (VR), microscopy, data encryption, communication, augmented reality (AR) technology and so on. However, still many potential applications of polarization-independent broadband meta-holographic thin films are greatly restricted due to polarization sensitivity and bandwidth trade-offs caused by the limited choice of constituent meta-atom geometries and materials. Moreover, current design strategies rely on the mergence of geometric and propagation phases, leading to complex design schemes, high computational costs, and fabrication challenges. Here in this research article, a simple and novel design strategy is proposed for broadband polarization-insensitive meta-holographic display using a single element in the optical regime. The proposed metasurface is constituent of new high refractive indexed based lossless dielectric material new hydrogenated amorphous silicon (new-H:aSi) based anisotropic nano-rectangular waveguides. Silicon dioxide (SiO2) is used as the transparent substrate for the designed metasurface. The geometric or PB phase (single degree of freedom) is utilized to attain control over entire phase range i.e. 0 to 2π. For authentication of the proposed concept, the designed metasurface is simulated and evaluated for three distinct visible wavelengths (i.e. 488nm, 532nm, and 633nm) which confirms the highly efficient broadband optical response. Thus, the proposed design approach based on photonic spin-orbit interactions with the features of high efficiency and bandwidth has raised hopes for many interesting applications of data storage, imaging, optical communication, and so on.

articleTitle: Development of EMD-Based Framework for Modeling the Effects of Chiropractic Care
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Chiropractic treatments form an emerging field in the domain of pain management. They are based on improving the way a human brain controls and the way all muscles work in coordination. In this research, We have used 64-channel highdensity surface EMG (HDSEMG) signals to quantify the changes before and after a single session of chiropractic intervention. we have proposed an EMD-based signal decomposition in combination with statistical features to magnify and locate the changes post-treatment. To nullify the random changes that may have occurred due to musculoskeletal variations we have utilized paired t-test with 5% significance to separate the most significant features from random variations.

articleTitle: Transition Maneuver Optimization of a Hybrid UAV Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In the past few years, the increasing need for dynamic mission profiles of UAVs has led to the development of autonomous aerial vehicles with sophisticated path planning, tracking, and control algorithms. Owing to the size and aerodynamic structure of small UAVs, they can achieve maneuvers like VTOL (Vertical Take off and Landing) and transition maneuvers from hover to cruise mode. Trajectory optimization of such maneuvers helps to minimize flight time and path while considering spatial constraints. The emergence of Machine Learning has gained attention for developing control systems based on such algorithms. This study mainly explores the algorithm Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) for path planning and optimization. To enhance the capabilities of small UAVs, a hybrid tiltrotor aircraft model is considered, which aims to hover and transition to an efficient forward flight during the cruise.

articleTitle: Compact High Gain, High Isolation, and Ultra-broadband AMC-based MIMO Antenna for 5G Millimetre Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research paper presents high-gain and ultra-broadband multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for 5G millimetre wave communication systems. The single unit of the MIMO attains a wideband response in a minimal footprint through a partially grounded slotted patch structure. Spatial and polarization diversity schemes are used to design a highly uncoupled four-port MIMO antenna. The gain of the four-port MIMO antenna is significantly improved (up to 3 times) by coupling it to a 14 × 12 artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) array. The designed prototype is fabricated and tested. The prototype achieves the feats of large bandwidth (22–34 GHz), high peak gain (8.54 dBi), and high isolation (<-25 dB) in a compact layout. The listed credentials are ideal for 5G communication networks and devices.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Printed Dipole Antenna with Wide Azimuth Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A novel dual-polarized (DP) printed dipole antenna with wide azimuth beamwidth for both, vertical and horizontal, polarizations is presented in this paper. For a vertically polarized (VP) dipole having H-plane along azimuth direction, the azimuth beamwidth is readily wide. However, for horizontally polarized (HP) dipole, the azimuth beamwidth is made wide by incorpo-rating two patches between printed dipole and ground plane. The inclusion of patches increases the azimuth beamwidth of HP dipole at the expense of some gain loss. The performance of the proposed antenna design is validated by fabricating a DP antenna and measuring its radiation characteristics. Peak realized gains of 7.53 and 6.3 dBi are obtained, respectively, for VP and HP dipole with azimuth beamwidth greater than 90° for both polarizations.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Buffet-Causing Phenomenon in Hammerhead Shaped Body
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Buffeting is a phenomenon that occurs in transonic regime due to pressure fluctuations in the flow. It usually occurs at low frequencies and can cause the vehicle system to collapse if the frequencies meet with the natural frequency of the system causing resonance. Usually fore-body flow is more susceptible to these loads. In this article, the loads in the form of pressure fluctuations are determined for a wind-tunnel tested body called as Model 11 (examined earlier by NASA). This body is an ideal candidate for buffeting study due to its shape. The results are numerically validated with the experimental study by NASA. For validations, Mach 0.84 and 1.17 were selected for comparison. Delayed Detached Eddy Simulation (DDES) technique is used for resolving the flow. The results are overall comparable with experimental findings, with the difference in the critical region due to unresolved flow characteristics. It was observed that with DDES technique the flow phenomenon is obtainable with some difference due to the limitations of the technique. These results can be used as a benchmark in development of an indigenous design of a launch vehicle.

articleTitle: Recognition of Urdu Handwritten Words Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Cursive hand script recognition is reported as a problematic task in words recognition due to variations in writing styles from person to person. Urdu script has related challenges comparable to Arabic script due to the complex ligatures. To cope with these issues, we proposed to use deep learning (DL) techniques i.e., transfer learning and ensemble learning. A novel dataset was generated which comprised 2496 images of Urdu handwritten words by 26 different writers and 288 images of computer-generated words. The whole dataset contained 96 classes. The data augmentation technique was used to add diversity and increase the dataset size to 13,920 images. To thoroughly evaluate the results of this study, a comparative analysis of the accomplishments was carried out. Among all the applied DL models, the ensemble learning model produced the best results as compared to state-of-the-art models. The proposed model moves handwritten words recognition to a higher level and can efficiently be automated.

articleTitle: CB-UNet: A Channel Boosted UNet Architecture for Lymphocyte Detection in Histopathological Images
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Accurate identification and segmentation of cancer cell nuclei from histopathological images is of vital importance in efficient cancer diagnosis and treatment. Problems in manual segmentation raised the need for automated lymphocyte detection as manual techniques are time-consuming, error-prone, and are more subjected to pathologists conflict. Much work have been done previously in automated detection of lymphocyte. In this study, we propose a unique architecture called CB-UNet for nuclei segmentation in cancer histopathology images. Our approach, CB-UNet utilizes the concept of “channel boosting,” employing multiple encoders to enhance the input channels and generate diverse and informative feature maps. By merging these feature maps and passing them through a decoder layer, we generate high-resolution segmentation masks. We evaluated our model's performance using evaluation metrics such as Intersection over Union (IOU) and Dice coefficient on the Lysto dataset and the MonuSeg dataset. These metrics demonstrate the superiority of our proposed architecture, CB-UNet, over existing methods. The results highlight the enhanced precision and effectiveness of nuclei segmentation for cancer diagnosis and treatment. This study signifies an advancement in nuclei segmentation techniques, with the potential to improve the overall treatment of cancer patients.

articleTitle: Design of Microstrip Based Miniature Highly Selective Bandpass Filter for Radio & Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband bandpass filter (BPF) with wideband stopband performance and higher selectivity is presented. The transmission response resembles a highly desirable sharp brick type. The design implemented in microstrip technology outperforms waveguides with comparable properties while significantly reducing its cost, dimensions, and weight. It has a center frequency (CF) of 3 GHz with upper and lower cut-off frequencies of 2.49 GHz and 3.53 GHz, respectively, and offers wideband suppression in both upper and lower stopbands. The fabricated filter has an insertion loss (IL) of 0.9 dB, bearing 3 dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) and selectivity of 34.55 and 78.8 percent, respectively. Its fabrication is simple and affordable for mass production due to its small size and via-free structure. Both simulated and measured results are in excellent harmony. The proposed filter is suitable for air traffic control radar application.

articleTitle: Heat Conduction Based Topological Design Evaluation for Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Topology optimization is an effective technique for designing optimal material distributions within a given domain to achieve desired performance. This paper is based on the evaluation of a heat conduction based optimized design for additive manufacturing by using three popular topology optimization methods namely: the Solid Isotropic Material with Penalization (SIMP) method, the Level Set (LS) method and the Radial Basis Function (RBF) based level set method. For all these methods, the equations related to the thermal system are solved with finite element method for evolution of topological sensitivities. The optimization formulation comprises of heat transfer potential as an objective function and the maximum material volume as a design constraint. The optimal designs obtained are critically evaluated with respect to the requirements of additive manufacturing. Several numerical examples with different loads and constraints are presented to compare the performance of the three topology optimization methods in terms of the quality of optimized designs that are appropriate for additivemanufacturing.

articleTitle: Software Reliability Analysis Using Prediction Models
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Software Reliability analysis plays a vital role to ensure quality and dependability of software systems. In order to achieve desired reliability of a software product, reliability prediction in early phases of software development life cycle is beneficial for effective resource allocation, risk assessment, and decision-making. These early decisions benefit in twofold, firstly, they supplement software reliability directly and secondly, reduce rework cost associated with bug fixes at later stages. In this research, we studied different approaches of software reliability prediction and applied Neufelder's Shortcut Model on real projects to evaluate its effectiveness and usefulness. The prediction models are based on historical failure data capturing complex dependencies and relationships among various factors directly influencing software reliability. Both Reliability Prediction and Reliability Growth Estimation models (can be used after testing phase) have their own advantages but the prediction models have an advantage over estimation models that they can predict reliability early in project life cycle enabling corrective decision in a proactive manner to achieve the desired reliability in a more deliberate way. We collected real software metrics for Neufelder's shortcut model of different projects to predict defect density and software reliability. Their effectiveness is evaluated using the designer's assessment and growth estimation based on the failure data of the software products. The results demonstrate that software reliability prediction models can be useful for developer, QA engineer, reliability engineer and at the same time for customers for pre-assessment of software reliability of the desired product. Overall, our research contributes to the advancement for software reliability analysis and empowering organizations to build more reliable and robust software system.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of the Effect of Inlet Total Pressure on H2/Air Non-premixed Rotating Detonation Combustor
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In order to comprehensively analyze the operational characteristics of the rotating detonation combustor (RDC) with separate fuel (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and oxidizer (air) supply under real conditions and provide guidance for the RDC design, a reduced kinetic mechanism based on the 8-step reaction and 7 species was utilized to simulate the three-dimensional flow field characteristics of the RDC. Detailed investigations were conducted on the impact of air inlet total pressure on fuel-oxidizer mixing and the propagation characteristics of the detonation wave (DW). The blocking effects of the DW characterized by high peak pressure on the upstream flow in the axial direction were also examined. The results reveal that the flow field within the RDC can be divided into five distinct zones: the fresh mixture-filled region, the combustion product region within the detonation cycle, the combustion product region compressed by oblique shock wave, the combustion product region from the previous detonation cycle, and the contact combustion region. As the air inlet total pressure increases, both the peak pressure of the DW and the blocking effect on the air inlet are strengthened, while the velocity of the DW decreases. Specifically, when the total pressure rises from 0.4MPa to 0.8MPa, the range of variation for the blocking ratio of the air mass flow rate extends from 0.35-0.45 to 0.2-0.63, and the velocity of the DW reduces from 1974 m/s to 1430 m/s. Higher air inlet total pressure results in a more pronounced blocking effect on the incoming flow and increased instability for the DW propagation process.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on Working Process of Gas-filled Accumulator
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Gas-filled accumulator is the key technology of oxygen pressurization system, which has successfully achieved pogo stabilization in several launch vehicles. Previous research on the gas-filled accumulator relies a lot on the lumped parameters method, where many factors need to be simplified in the process of modeling and analysis. In this research, a computational fluid dynamics model, based on Navier-Stokes equation and RNG <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k-\varepsilon$</tex> model, is established for simulation research on a simplified gas-filled accumulator injecting with gaseous oxygen. Volume of Fluid method is used to track the volume fraction for liquid oxygen free-surface inside the accumulator, where the gaseous phase is regarded ideal and the liquid phase is considered incompressible. The accumulator worked for 10s under oscillating pressure with an amplitude of 0.1 MPa and a frequency of 10 Hz, while the ullage has four different working conditions. The result shows that there will be a periodic fluctuation of liquid level inside the accumulator if the flow difference of injection and exhaust gaseous oxygen flow rate is not large enough. But excessive flow difference will cause the reduction of ullage volume, thus reducing the accumulator compliance. And without any liquid management method, the propellant inside the accumulator will splash, resulting gas babbles being mixed with the propellant, and sucked into communication ports periodically due to the vortex inside the liquid domain. The simulation result also indicate that the vertical flow of the mainstream will compress the flow area of communication ports, causing the linear resistance of the accumulator to be larger than the estimated value of the orifice flow model. This study provides a research reference for the design and application of gas-filled accumulator.

articleTitle: LPNOsc: An X-band Low-Phase-Noise Oscillator Based on Complementary Coupled Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Low-phase microwave oscillators are one of the key components in modern radars for frequency conversion and signal generation. However, it is challenging to design low-phase microwave oscillators while meeting other requirements, i.e., low-profile, low cost, and good DC-RF conversion. Therefore, the manuscript presents an oscillator designed on the complementary coupled resonator (CCR) technique with low-phase noise for X-band applications to address this challenge. The substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is used for the planar resonator design because of its simple integration with other components. The SIW-based CCR resonators have a high unloaded quality factor (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), The proposed oscillator produced an output RF signal with 9.77 dBm signal strength at 10 GHz frequency. The CCR resonator has Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> of 3030 and coupling coefficient (C) value of 1.069. The high figure of merit (FOM) value of -203.5 dBc/Hz and the low-phase noise -141.7 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset are the key features of the proposed oscillator that make it an appealing candidate for X-band applications.

articleTitle: Estimation of 3 DOF Position Trajectory of AUV by Extended Kalman Filter using Inertial Navigation Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Many jobs were impossible for manned vehicles to complete in the treacherous subsea environment. The advance-ment of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) has allowed for unprecedented levels of exploration, monitoring, and study. AUVs are increasingly widely utilized for long missions, but because of water currents and oceanic complexity, they have difficulty maintaining an accurate position over a wider operational region. As a result, AUVs need more advanced navigational systems. However, the degradation of GPS and radio signals makes underwater navigation difficult. In this work of research, an Extended Kalman filter (EKF) with an inertial navigation system (INS) is proposed for precise location estimation of an AUV in three degrees of freedom (DOF). The EKF is used to simulate a sample of the INS accelerometer's data in the MATLAB environment to calculate position from acceleration, and the double integration technique of finding position is contrasted. The results of our experiments indicate that the suggested strategy yields better outcomes.

articleTitle: A Numerical Study on Effect of Ceramic Core Placement on Composites Under Impact
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research work presents the numerical study of damage analysis of composite materials under impact loadings. Low velocity numerical study has been performed on composite sandwich core structure of [Kevlar (±45°) / Alumina Core / Kevlar (±45°)], to analyze the damage behavior, delamination and energy absorption behavior due to placement of ceramic sandwich core. Numerical simulations were performed using Abaqus Explicit 6.13. Hashin failure criteria is employed for damage prediction with the implication of cohesive zone modeling. It is analyzed that delamination is preceded by matrix cracking. Delamination starts at the center and propagates outwards along lower ply fiber direction at the interface. Similar behavior is noticed for fiber tensile damage. However, damage area of delamination increases with increasing level of impact energy. Moreover, energy absorption increases significantly with placement of ceramic sandwich core as compared to pure composite panel.

articleTitle: Drone Detection and Classification on Micro-Doppler Signatures Using FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Drone detection and classification has become of great importance due to its increasing potential threats. These drones are unable to be detected using conventional radars techniques due to small RCS, hovering feature, slow speed and low altitudes. The micro-Doppler signatures depending on the rotation of rotor blades allow us to differentiate various types of drones. Radars signals reflected from hovering drones have zero Doppler shift therefore remain undetected by conventional radars. This paper focuses on drone detection and classification using FMCW radar kit with implementation of micro-doppler feature. Experimental data was collected using Tinyrad24G FMCW radar kit. Firstly, the time-frequency spectrograms are obtained by performing the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) on the radar data. The experimental investigation is conducted to analyze different micro-doppler signatures for different commercial drones in different frequency bands, with the aim to clearly distinguish drone from other flying targets with similar characteristics. Three drones utilized for the experiment are DJI Mini, DJI Mini2 and DJI Mavic Classic 3. All the drones utilized exhibit small RCS value less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.01\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> and maximum blade length of 0.10m. We further classify the frequency components along with number of blades in order to identify the drones signature. Our results demonstrate the applicability of the technique in identification of hovering drones without loss of target in real time.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Framework for Automated Vulnerability Detection in Android Applications
