publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Identifying vulnerabilities is essential for safeguarding software systems against cyber attacks. It becomes particularly crucial to pinpoint the specific vulnerable functions within the source code to facilitate their remediation. Nonetheless, this process is both challenging and time-consuming, demanding specialized security expertise. Also, the publicly available vulnerability datasets are relatively scarce. To address the issue we propose a systematic, language-independent framework for automated vulnerability detection in applications. We have curated a large dataset of open-source binaries containing both vulnerable and non-vulnerable samples. This dataset is labelled using relevant findings from hybrid analyzer that highlight potential exploit indicators, aiming to enhance existing labeled vulnerability datasets which is publicly available. Deep learning methodology is applied to detect potential vulnerabilities by treating source code extracted from large number of binaries as natural language text. We employ the word tokenizer with CNN and BERT tokenizer with CNN models to detect function-level vulnerabilities in real source code. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in accurately identifying vulnerabilities in source code, thereby enhancing the protection of applications against cyber attacks.

articleTitle: Detrimental Influence of Carbon Enrichment in TiO2 Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Carbon-modified <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> has been predicted as a promising candidate for a diverse range of applications such as photocatalysis, photoelectrochemistry, and energy storage and conversion. So far, the synergistic beneficial effect of carbon has been studied and reported, yet higher concentrations of carbon can produce detrimental effects such as inefficient charge separation resulting in a decreased efficiency in photo electrochemical applications. Such detrimental effects of carbon enrichment have not been investigated in detail, remaining an essential factor. This study highlights the impact of carbon enrichment on the properties and performance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> nanotubes (NTs). First, the NTs were investigated by SEM, EDX, XPS, and Raman analysis to characterize their morphology and composition. The obtained carbon-modified <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> NTs were used as photoelectrodes demonstrating a 2 times decrease in the IPCE efficiency compared to pristine NTs. Understanding the detrimental effect of carbon enrichment on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> NT performance by advancing their synthesis and optimization strategies is vital for maximizing their efficiency in photocatalytic applications.

articleTitle: Pixels to Precision: Features Fusion and Random Forests over Labelled-based Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Object classification is a crucial yet challenging vision ability to perfect The fundamental objective is to educate computers to understand visuals the same way humans do. Due to variables like brightness, distance, and backdrop that affect object appearance and recognition, disagreements about accurate object categorization still exist despite tremendous advances. In this paper, the initial preprocessing attempts to carry out comes before any later analyses. Following this preprocessing stage, the image will be divided into several sections based on hue similarity. Following methodical alteration, these segmented portrayals will be reduced to their essential components in order to make it easier to recognize the target object. The Random Forest algorithm's use for classification purposes is described in depth, leading to an overall accuracy rate of 89.70%.

articleTitle: Telemonitoring of Daily Activities Based on Multi-Sensors Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Multi-sensor data fusion has played a crucial role in a wide range of daily life activities including smart homes, sports, healthcare, and so on. This work has presented a telemonitoring approach for the recognition of daily life activities by analyzing multi-sensor data including depth, inertial, and RGB sensors. Combining multiple sensors enhances the accuracy of daily life activities, as each sensor captures the unique detail of human activities. The RGB sensors provide information about object appearance and visual cues. The depth sensors disseminate information on 3D spatial and geometric. The inertial sensors impart knowledge about the angle and orientation details of each motion. The prescribed methodology is based on multi-sensor data preprocessing, feature extraction, data fusion, data optimization, and classification. The prescribed method has achieved an optimal accuracy of 98.32% and 98.03% on Berkeley MHAD and UTD-MHAD standard datasets. The proposed model has outperformed the classification results over cutting-edge models. The prescribed methodology could be an opportunity for an IoT-based solution, to optimize the activities of daily living through seamless integration. The prescribed methodology can be further used in developing intelligent systems to detect human behavior and improve interactive responsiveness between humans and technology.

articleTitle: Robust Hand Gesture Tracking and Recognition for Healthcare via Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In the emerging fields of computer vision, robotics, and medicine, It's difficult to recognize gestures in dynamic environment. For human-computer hand gesture tracking and recognition, symmetry is required. Recent research has presented many RGB gesture recognition methods as a result of sensor technology advancements. In this research, we propose a sustainable hand gesture tracking and recognition system that can identify and recognize RGB dynamic motions in challenging environments while maintaining accuracy. Firstly, the frames are extracted from dynamic gestures. The frames are preprocessed to reduce noise and adjust light intensity. After that, the hand is detected using the Single-shot Multi-box Detector (SSD). From the extracted hand landmarks are attained via a colour-based fast marching algorithm. The features are extracted, such as polygon mesh, neural gas, and geometric shapes. On the features, the Active Bee Colony Optimizer (ABCO) is applied to reduce dimensionality. Then Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) is applied to classify the gestures. The proposed system is tested on Sign word and Egogesture datasets, providing accuracy of 93.33% and 92.67%, respectively.

articleTitle: Nonlinear MPPT Algorithm for PV System Using a Condition Based Supertwisting Sliding Mode Control and Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Due to increasing desire for energy, dwindling fossil assets, and effects of carbon-dioxide emissions, there is a need of replacement for efficient, and environmentally accountable ecosystem. Solar energy enchant widespread interest in the realm of inexhaustible energy-system in recent years. Immense ability of a photovoltaic (PV) generation is affected by climatic circumstances and fluctuations in the load. Due to drastic changes in climate, solar energy has poor efficiency. To overcome it most well-known field of research is obtaining maximum electricity through maximum power point tracking (MPPT). MPPT is utilized as the key to creating effective solar PV systems. The performance of the controller in MPPT can increase PV's system-driven efficiency. The characteristics of PV system are highly nonlinear, so non-linear control is more suited for MPPT applications. For (MPPT) analysis getting the greatest power, different methods have been employed in the literature, such as incremental-conductance (INC), and perturb and observed (PO). Recently with the innovation in the artificial intelligence sector more useful techniques like artificial neural networks (ANN) is widely used. MPPT must be ensured by a robust controller, which manages a system's nonlinearities and assembles it to resilient changing environmental conditions. This paper's objective is to monitor the reference of PV voltage upto covet value using the MPPT techniques, e.g Fuzzy-Logic (FL), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Non-linear condition-based super twisting sliding mode (CST-SMC) control. The precision of the peak reference determines the MPPT efficiency of a PV system. An essential use of an offline-trained artificial neural network is needed to create the reference for peak power voltage, that monitored and executed by the nonlinear controllers. To compare with the proposed controllers, a super-twisting sliding mode (ST-SMC) controller is also designed for MPPT/PV system. The hardware-in-Ioop (HIL) based experimental results verify the real-time control of the proposed controller. Decisive comparisons of MPPT are shown by simulations between fuzzy logic controller, perturb and observed and incremental conductance's.

articleTitle: Modelling, Simulation, and Control of a Flexible Space Launch Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Modern Space Launch Vehicles (SLVs), being slender in shape and due to the use of lightweight materials, are generally flexible in nature. This structural flexibility, when coupled with sensor and actuator dynamics, can adversely affect the control of SLV, which may lead to vehicle instability and, in the worst-case scenario, to structural failure. This work focuses on modelling and simulation of rigid and flexible dynamics of an SLV and its interactions with the control system. SpaceX's Falcon 9 has been selected for this study. The flexible modes are calculated using modal analysis in Ansys. High-fidelity nonlinear simulation is developed which incor-porates the flexible modes and their interactions with rigid degrees of freedom. Moreover, linearized models are developed for flexible body dynamics, over the complete trajectory until the first stage's separation. Using classical control methods, attitude controllers, that keep the SLV on its desired trajectory, are developed, and multiple filters are designed to suppress the interactions of flexible dynamics. The designed controllers along with filters are implemented in the nonlinear simulation. Furthermore, to demonstrate the robustness of designed controllers, Monte-Carlo simulations are carried out and results are presented.

articleTitle: A Q-Learning-Based Multi-Hop Energy-Efficient and Low Collision MAC Protocol for Underwater Acoustic Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Underwater acoustic wireless sensor networks (UAWSNs) are being confess as a valuable tool for studying and monitoring aquatic environments. However, the unique characteristics of acoustic communication in UAWSNs present significant challenges. These challenges include high latency, which refers to delays in transmitting data, low available bandwidth, which limits the amount of data that can be transmitted, and a high bit error rate, which refers to errors that occur during the transmission of data. Addressing these aforementioned challenges is critical to the successful deployment and operation of UAWSNs for environmental monitoring and other applications. Contention-based medium access control (MAC) protocols are not suited for use in UAWSNs because to their lower efficiency as compared to terrestrial networks because of the distinctive attributes of UAWSNs. To address this issue, a contention-free MAC protocol is deemed more suitable, as it offers greater reliability and flexibility in overcoming the challenges posed by acoustic signals. This protocol may also increase the network's throughput and energy efficiency by removing the potential of collisions, thereby achieving high performance. In this research, we proposed a new multi-hop energy-efficient and low collision MAC protocol using Q-learning technique for UAWSNs. The proposed MAC protocol is designed to address the challenges of UAWSNs, such as low available bandwidth, high latency, and high bit error rate. By utilizing a Q-learning approach, the protocol is able to make informed decisions in selecting the optimal communication path while minimizing energy consumption and reducing the occurrence of collisions. This is achieved through a multi-hop approach that allows for efficient data transmission across the network. The protocol's energy efficiency and collision avoidance capabilities make it a promising candidate for use in various underwater applications, including environmental monitoring, underwater surveillance, and exploration. The simulation results demonstrate that the suggested MAC protocol outperformed other schemes in terms of throughput, collision rates, and energy efficiency. This suggests that the suggested approach is successful in fixing the problems with UAWSNs and may enhance the performance of the entire network.

articleTitle: Estimation of Power System Harmonics Using Least Square Based Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Harmonic distortion stands out as a significant power quality issue in contemporary power systems that experience extensive utilization of renewable energy sources. This concern has garnered increased focus in recent years due to the growing integration of power electronic devices and nonlinear loads within the power systems. For electric utilities and users, accurate estimation of harmonic-parameters is an important reference to evaluate power quality. The detrimental impacts of harmonics components on power systems can be effectively mitigated by Active Filters (AFs). The performance of AFs heavily relies on the development of robust and accurate estimator, which plays a vital role in supplying the necessary reference harmonic values. This paper presents a Least Square based Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (LS-AOA) to solve the harmonics estimation problem. The AOA leverages the distribution characteristic of main arithmetic operators, such as division, subtraction, multiplication and addition in mathematics. AOA is mathematically formulated and implemented to efficiently optimize search processes across diverse ranges. The proposed LS-AOA framework is tested and validated on benchmark test signals with different noise levels and on practically measured voltage waveform of AFPMG. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed harmonic estimator provides more accurate estimations with significantly lower computational time compared to existing techniques proposed in literature.

articleTitle: Enhanced Tuberculosis Treatment and Prevention Using Genetic Algorithm Based Control Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is a highly perilous infectious disease triggered by the bacteria known as mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB). It primarily impacts the lungs but can also invade and affect various other organs and body parts. Researchers have extensively utilized the susceptible, exposed, infected, recovered, and resistant (SEIRS) model to enhance their understanding of TB transmission dynamics. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing the controllers, like proportional integral derivative (PID) and sliding mode control (SMC). The objective is to devise effective treatment strategies to reduce the number of infected individuals while simultaneously employing vaccination to prevent disease transmission among susceptible and exposed individuals. A genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to optimize the gains of the proposed controller, utilizing the integral time absolute error as the objective function. The stability of the proposed controllers is demonstrated through mathematical analysis using the Lyapunov stability criteria. Performance comparisons of the controllers are conducted using MATLAB/Simulink simulations, while a hardware-in-loop experimental setup involving the C2000 Delfino and MCU F28379D Launchpad is utilized for real-time scenario validation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Smartphone Positioning Accuracy Through Optimal GNSS Setup and Correction Data Configuration: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation on the setup and configuration of the Samsung A23 smartphone as a rover for precise positioning applications. By leveraging the smartphone's built-in GNSS capabilities, including support for multiple satellite systems, dual-frequency signals, and assisted GPS, we explore the potential to achieve highly accurate positioning results. Specifically, we focus on the role of a base station in providing correction data to mitigate signal errors and improve positioning reliability. Additionally, we employ RTKLIB software for GNSS data collection and processing to enhance accuracy. The study involves comparing the visibility and dilution of precision (DOP) values across various mask angles to assess the quality of the GNSS positioning solutions. Through this research, we aim to identify optimal configurations and strategies that can significantly enhance the accuracy of rover positioning, benefiting fields such as land surveying, precision agriculture, and autonomous navigation.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Channel States Analysis in Evolved Cellular Networks Using Probabilistic Model Checking
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The 5th generation (5G) of cellular networks plays a vital role in providing wireless connectivity for a variety of market verticals and in meeting industry revolution (IR 4.0) targets. High capacity and improved quality of service are among the key performance parameters required by a variety of applications in 5G networks. To meet the high capacity goal, the mmWave carrier frequencies spectrum has been selected due to the enormous bandwidth available in this frequency spectrum. But, the radio wave propagation in mmWave poses a big challenge in achieving reliable radio link connectivity for 5G users. In this paper, we model mmWave radio frequency (RF) channel states for heterogeneous networks under different coverage and capacity scenarios. We use a statistical RF pathloss based probabilistic channel model as well as a Markovian RF channel state model to analyze the dynamic nature of mmWave channel states. We employ probabilistic model checking, a formal verification technique, to analyze these RF channel states models. We compare these models and provide useful insights into mmWave RF channel states of 5G HetNets. Moreover, to analyze the 5G end-user experience, we provide a reward-based quantitative analysis of handover distribution for mobile 5G users moving in a two-layer heterogeneous network.

articleTitle: Enhanced Variational Quantum Regression for Non-Linear Curve Fitting in Higher Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The advent of quantum computing, characterized by limited resources and qubits, the large circuit depth presents a substantial challenge for quantum algorithms designed to solve linear systems of equations. This paper proposes an innovative approach, named Enhanced Variational Quantum Regression (EVQR), specifically designed for solving non-linear curve fitting problems in higher dimensions and orders. It is a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm which not only surpasses the limitations of traditional one-dimensional solvers but also leverages variational principles to address complex problems. Our methodology centers around an initial solution known as an “ansatz” parameterized by a function. By employing quantum circuits, qubits are prepared to efficiently compute inner products in the quantum domain, facilitating accelerated and powerful calculations. The estimated inner product is then transmitted back to the classical computer, where classical optimization techniques such as Levenberg-Marquardt are employed to estimate the function parameters. This iterative process is repeated until the estimation reaches a desired level of accuracy within a predefined tolerance. Notably, we empirically observe that the time complexity of EVQR scales efficiently with the system size N. By leveraging the capabilities of SciPy's curve-fit and the robust optimization techniques of the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, our approach overcomes the challenge of higher-dimensional curve fitting. Our primary contribution lies in the fusion of quantum and classical methodologies, a novel integration that, unlike previous quantum approaches, outperforms in terms of performance and accuracy. By combining the strengths of classical optimization and quantum computations, EVQR offers a versatile framework for solving challenging problems, opening new possibilities for data analysis & modeling.

articleTitle: Electro-Mechanical Behavior of Hybrid Composite Sandwich Radome: A-Type Radome
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Today, Sandwich composite radomes are being used in fighter aircrafts, drones, UAV's and missiles. Generally radome structure can be monolayer, two layer, three layer (A-Type) and five layer (C-Type). For current study, a multidisciplinary design process for manufacturing hybrid sandwich composite A-type radomes is presented. The methodology is composed of two parallel setups for testing of electromagnetic behavior and mechanical properties of selected materials, which are simultaneously essential for the better performance of radome. The design process begins with the choice of an appropriate material to satisfy the service requirements, such as EMI transparency and structural integrity against aerodynamic loads. To choose the appropriate material and core foam, the Multi Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) method was also used. The MCDM assigns ranking to the materials to be chosen in order to satisfy functional requirements. Accordingly full scale nose radome of a flight vehicle (<0.8 Mach) was manufactured utilizing hand-layup technique assisted by vacuum bagging using SGlass/PMI Foam/Kevl<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> and low viscosity epoxy. The full scale radome was tested to check EMI behavior (X-band frequencies) by free space measurement method. EMI response was found satisfying the requirements (as per MIL R-7705B) Furthermore, to ensure that selected materials and layup sequence will fulfil structural performance requirements of Radome, multiple specimens were prepared adhering same stacking sequence as that of the Radome. Mechanical testing of specimens was carried out in accordance of ASTM Standard for flexure and tensile testing (ASTM D7246/D760 and ASTM D3039, respectively). Tensile strength of S-Glass and Kevlar was found 263 MPa and 335 MPa respectively, and flexural strength was 351 MPa and 336 MPa, respectively. The flexural testing was also done of sandwich samples comprises, as per ASTM D7246, of S-glass / Foam / Kevlar in accordance 3x ply/4mm/3x ply and 200 gsm in weight for both facing fabrics and found 20 MPa Strength. It is concluded that manufactured A-type Radome, using the selected materials through MCDM technique, has performed well to satisfy the requisite EMI and mechanical requirements.

articleTitle: Modulation Recognition of the OFDM Signals in the UAV-RIS Based AI-enabled 6G Network for Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and 6G networks aims to enhance agricultural applications by enabling adaptive and efficient communication systems. Fusing the potential and strengths of machine learning (ML) technology and the high-speed, low-latency communication capabilities of 6G networks, we can create intelligent farming systems that can enhance productivity, reduce resource wastage, and ensure sustainable agricultural practices. To tackle resource wastage and power efficiency of 6G-enabled devices, we present an AI-based solution that utilizes pre-trained Deep Learning (DL) models to classify Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) modulated Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) signals. The proposed approach involves recognizing signals based on the classification results at the receiving nodes, prompting them to switch their radio modulation schemes to options such as 4-QAM, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM. Taking advantage of DL models for QAM classification and dynamically adjusting modulation schemes, the proposed solution can optimize resource utilization, improve data transmission quality, and enhance overall network performance in agricultural applications. We used pre-trained ResNet50, MobileNetV2, and a scratch CNN model. Our results show that pretrained models performed better than scratch CNN models and demonstrate the feasibility of using pretrained DL models for modulation scheme classification, offering promising opportunities for the development of adaptive and intelligent agricultural systems.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Movie Reviews Using Improved Word2Vec and CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The concept of sentiment analysis is spreading across multiple fields including business, politics, movies, religion, academia, etc. Sentiment analysis is a very challenging job, and the accurate prediction of sentiments is very problematic. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) and an enhanced word vector (Word2Vec) were utilized to do sentiment analysis on movie reviews. Word embedding is created in the initial stage using Word2Vec and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA). Then CNN is implemented on the pre-trained word vectors for binary class sentiment analysis of movie reviews. The suggested model's accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were tested on a publicly available dataset from Stanford University (Movie Review Database), and they were 0.924, 0.932, and 0.924, respectively, And The results indicate that the improved Word2Vec is not only used to gain the word vectors but also improves the feature representation ability of the model by fusing both the local and global connections. The proposed method outperformed all the baseline methods for sentiment analysis of movie reviews.

articleTitle: Foliar Diseases Identification in Apple Tree Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Apple is a popular fruit crop that is susceptible to a variety of foliar diseases. In apple trees detecting foliar diseases is a critical aspect of orchard management, as it can prevent yield losses and maintain food security. Currently, disease detection is carried out through manual inspection and visual assessment, which can be time-consuming, subjective, and prone to errors. Early and precise recognition of these diseases is significant for effective disease management. The proposed methodology involves digital images of apple leaves, preprocessing the images, segmentation, and training a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model to recognize the visual patterns associated with different foliar diseases. The model's accuracy, precision, and recall are used to analyze how well it performs. The results indicate that our approach is better able to achieve high accuracy in identifying various foliar diseases in apple trees. The proposed approach can provide a reliable, and accurate tool for apple growers to monitor the health status of their trees and take timely action against diseases.

articleTitle: Detection of Internet Layer DoS Attack on Cloud Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Attacks on cloud infrastructure and services have become a significant concern due to the increasing reliance on cloud computing. Various types of attacks pose threats to the cloud ecosystem. Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks aim to disrupt services by overwhelming the cloud infrastructure with excessive traffic, rendering them inaccessible. Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks take this a step further by utilizing a network of compromised devices to launch coordinated attacks, causing widespread disruptions. Traditional rule-based detection methods may struggle to keep pace with the sophistication and diversity of modern DoS attacks. Machine learning algorithms, on the other hand, can learn from historical attack data, network behavior, and anomalies to detect and classify malicious traffic accurately. In this paper, we propose a classifier based on deep learning algorithms that can detect modern sophisticated DoS attacks more accurately, enabling early detection and timely response. The proposed classifier demonstrated high detection rates, often exceeding 99%, in effectively identifying DoS attacks on cloud infrastructure.

articleTitle: Swarm Robots on a Mission: Optimizing Inspections with Fuzzy Logic and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Swarm robotics is a captivating paradigm where a multitude of miniature robots collaborate to perform complex tasks with precision and speed. Coordination is crucial for seamless collaboration, and advanced algorithms play a pivotal role in optimizing swarm robot behavior. This survey highlights the transformative impact of swarm robots in various domains, such as disaster zone exploration and gas leak detection, and underscores the significance of coordination in achieving efficient and effective outcomes. This research survey explores the im-portance of advanced algorithms, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC), in coordinating swarm robots. The objective is to investigate their potential applications and shed light on their methodologies.The survey delves into the methodologies of PSO and FLC algorithms, which contribute to optimizing swarm robot behavior. PSO fine-tunes the behavior of individual robots by iteratively updating their positions based on individual best positions, while FLC establishes a rule-based framework that governs the overall swarm behavior. By combining PSO and FLC, swarm robots excel in tasks requiring precision, speed, and adaptability, adapting to dynamic environments efficiently. Through a comprehensive literature review, the survey examines the coordination mechanisms facilitated by these algorithms. It highlights their potential applications, showcases their effectiveness in optimizing swarm robot behavior, and discusses the challenges and areas for improvement. This research survey investigates the combined potential of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) in swarm robotics. PSO alone may not suffice for efficient optimization, but when integrated with FLC, a powerful synergy emerges, enabling swarm robots to conduct highly efficient target searches. Utilizing advanced PSO variants becomes essential for optimal outcomes. The study emphasizes the applications and benefits of PSO and FLC in swarm robotics, contributing to advancements in the field. The findings demonstrate the potential for improved coordination, precision, speed, and adaptability in various domains. By leveraging the collective intelligence of swarm robots, this research opens doors to transformative real-world applications.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effectiveness of Joint Bi-LSTM-GNN vs ChatGPT-LLM in Source Code Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The ability to search for and retrieve important code snippets from huge codebases is a critical task in software engineering. Traditional approaches for retrieving source code rely on keyword-based queries, which might produce erroneous and partial results. As a result, scientists are investigating the use of deep learning approaches to enhance code search. In this study, a Joint Bi-LSTM-GNN (JBLG) model is proposed for source code search. This model combines the features of BiLSTM and GNN. This study also investigates the usage of Large Language Models (LLMs), notably ChatGPT, for source code retrieval in comparison with our proposed JBLG model for source code search. Our results reveal that our proposed JBLG model surpasses standard retrieval approaches and other deep learning models. The JBLG model is tested on CodeSearchNet dataset, which comprises query code pairs from open-source projects in a variety of programming languages. Our joint model obtains an impressive mean reciprocal rank (MRR) score, which represents a considerable improvement over the best-performing baseline model. Overall, our findings show that the ChatGPT model does not perform, and this might be due to ChatGPT being a language model developed for natural language processing tasks rather than code retrieval. To further enhance the effectiveness of the model, future approaches for this study include examining the usage of attention processes and more sophisticated deep learning techniques. The suggested approach might also be expanded to include more programming languages and software engineering functions including code summary and code completion.

articleTitle: Intelligent Monitoring for Elderly Well-Being: Deep Learning-Based Activity Recognition for Fall Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The aging population poses unique challenges in terms of healthcare and well-being, requiring innovative solutions to ensure the safety and quality of life for elderly individuals. This research focuses on applying deep learning techniques for activity recognition in tracking and monitoring the daily activities of elderly people. The current literature on the matter suggests that state-of-the-art models find it difficult to accurately distinguish between falling and laying down. The study proposes a unique solution by dividing the dataset into local and global tags with local tags representing labels that are based on the information of that particular frame while global tags represent labels of a frame that are the same for the entire video. By using this dataset structure, we employ two CNNs: EfficientNet, ResNet, and a Vision Transformer (ViT-B16). The method proposed achieved promising results, with EfficientNet successfully distinguishing between falling and non-falling events with high accuracy. The paper also discusses the remaining two models, their shortcomings, and potential solutions for future work. In conclusion, this research contributes to the field of elderly care by showcasing the potential of deep learning in real-time activity recognition, where intelligent monitoring systems adapt to the specific needs of elderly individuals, promoting their well-being and independence while providing essential support for caregivers and healthcare providers.

articleTitle: Integration of Deep Neural Networks and Local Mean Decomposition for Accurate Underwater Acoustic Channel Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Accurate estimation of underwater acoustic channel is crucial for reliable communication in harsh underwater conditions. However, because of the dynamic nature of the underwater acoustic channel, reliable estimation of underwater acoustic channel is difficult. To overcome this problem, we offer a new method for improving UWA channel estimations that combines Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) with Local Mean Decomposition (LMD). To efficiently understand the complicated relationships within the UWA channel data, our proposed technique integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) which captures both spatial and temporal dependencies by using the capabilities of both CNNs and RNN s, allowing for a comprehensive understanding of the UW A channel properties. In addition, we use LMD as a post-processing step at the receiver. LMD enables us to extract meaningful information from noisy signals, improving the accuracy of the estimated underwater acoustic channel. We can limit the negative impacts of noise and interference on received signals by successfully mitigating noise from them, resulting in increased performance. We performed simulations to compare the performance of our proposed model with conventional underwater acoustic channel estimation strategies. Results from simulations show that our approach surpasses these existing algorithms on key parameters including bit error rate (BER) and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). These results suggest that our technique has a lot of potential for enhancing the reliability and efficiency of underwater acoustic communication systems in complicated underwater environments. The implications of our proposed method are significant, since it allows for improved performance in severe underwater environments. Our method improves the overall reliability of underwater communication systems by giving more precise estimations of the underwater acoustic channel. This remarkable development has far-reaching implications, including greater efficiency, data throughput, and high-quality service in underwater applications such as underwater sensor networks, underwater robotics, and submarine communications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based 3D Reconstructed Objects via Generative Models and Octree Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Recent advancements in intelligent systems and innovative technology have revolutionized data processing, analysis, and reconstruction. Machine learning and artificial intelligence breakthroughs now enable the restoration of missing or lost information from datasets. However, reconstructing data lost during processes like image acquisition or dimension reduction remains a significant challenge. This study introduces a method that systematically captures 2D object images and predicts voxel-based 3D representations to reconstruct the objects. Using a multi-layer encoder and decoder, the image's depth is estimated and combined with the original image to determine the object's 3D shape. EfficientNet and an octree-based technique generate voxels from the 3D shape representation. The proposed model is evaluated on three benchmark datasets, comparing against state-of-the-art methods. Performance is assessed using evaluation metrics like Chamfer distance (CD), earth mover's distance (EMD), and intersection over union (IoU). Results indicate mean Chamfer distances of 0.00387, 0.00317, and 0.00102 for ShapeNetCore, Pascal3D+, and Pix3D, respectively. Mean IoU values of 5.58, 6.13, and 6.72 are achieved on the mentioned benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Deep Word Embedding and Language Model based Sentimental Analysis of COVID-19 Tweets
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The great Covid-19 pandemic affected billions of people's lives personally and socially. The research involves the analysis of public's views and opinions shared on Twitter social media platform related to Covid-19 pandemic and its detrimental or non-detrimental effects on public's mental health by using machine learning algorithm. The main purpose of this research includes analyzing public views related to Covid-19 pandemic by classifying the Tweets collected from the Twitter social platform. The proposed approach combines deep word embedding with MiniLM as an encoder to produce word vectors of high-dimensionality to preserve the words' semantic information. The resultant word vectors were used to train the model for the classification of the tweet in five sentiments i.e. Positive, Extremely Positive, Negative, Extremely Negative, and Neutral. The methodology is tested using publicly available Kaggle dataset as well as privately collected tweets. The comparative evaluation of the models revealed that MiniLM outperformed existing BERT based counterparts and attained highest accuracy of 93% with the Kaggle dataset. This analysis can assist the medical health authorities to monitor health information, conduct, and plan interventions to lower the pandemic effect and can help government to take precautionary measures.

articleTitle: Decoupling Data and Linguistic Knowledge for Spontaneous Tabular Q/A
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Recent advances in natural language processing and deep learning have opened thousands of new dimensions for transforming dreams into reality. One such dimension is Table Question-Answering (Q/A). It's an old fantasy of computer science to query tables in natural human language and extract the desired information. Currently, the subject is trending because a huge chunk of modern business data still exists in structured and semi-structured tables. The computational and hardware requirements of the problem linearly increase with the size and number of the provided tables, which makes it complex for real-time production environments. This challenging nature has raised the interest of new aspiring researchers in efficiently applying modern deep-learning tactics and developing systematically optimized solutions. In this paper, we aim to explore a sub-field of Table Question-Answering (Q/A) called Non-Semantic Closed-Domain Free-Form Table Question-Answering (Q/A) and develop a novel solution by decoupling the tabular data from linguistic knowledge. The goal of such decoupling is to enable the computational and resource optimizations that will benefit the scalability of the proposed system and allow the solution to function independently of the table size.

articleTitle: State Estimation for a Unicycle Robot Using Multi-Rate Sensor Fusion: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Autonomous systems, including unicycle robots, have attracted considerable interest across multiple domains, encompassing transportation, surveillance, and search-and-rescue missions. Achieving accurate state estimation is therefore crucial for the reliable and effective operation of these autonomous systems. This paper presents a comparative study on state estimation techniques for a unicycle robot using multi-rate sensor fusion. This work encompasses the evaluation of the Kalman Filter, Unscented Kalman Filter, Extended Kalman Filter, Set-Valued Kalman Filter, and Particle Filter to estimate the position, velocity, and orientation of a unicycle robot. The performance of these filtering techniques is compared for accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness in handling sensor measurements with different rates. The outcomes illustrate both the strengths and constraints inherent in each filtering algorithm, offering valuable perspectives on their appropriateness for performing state estimation in the context of unicycle robots, thus aiding researchers and developers in selecting the optimal method based on their specific requirements and constraints.

articleTitle: Self-Aware AI-Enabled Medical System
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The healthcare plays a critical role in lives of people, enhancing the quality of live and enabling growth of world economy. The healthcare providers rely on health monitoring devices to provide timely and accurate data that could be used for early diagnosis and intervention. However external interference and internal faults in these wireless medical devices can cause anomalies in the readings they provide. Moreover, these devices aren't self-aware due to which they provide inaccurate readings being without detecting them. Additionally, users remain unaware of the inaccurate readings and do not realize the potential consequences of these readings such as they might delay early diagnosis of emergency medical condition. In order to address these problems, we designed a framework named as Self-Aware AI-Enabled Medical System that employs machine learning and deep learning algorithms to make these devices self-aware. The framework enables these devices to detect interference and abnormalities in the data and it also incorporates an Early Warning Score (EWS) system that infers if a user's vitals suggest any emergency medical condition and alerts them for immediate medical assistance. In our framework, we have three major features, 1st feature is the initial model for prediction for which we have used LSTM. The 2nd the EWS model for which we have used Random Forest Classifier, and the 3rd feature is abnormality detection model for which we have used Support Vector Classifier (SVC). The framework was able to achieve an impressive overall accuracy rate of 94%. By making health monitoring devices selfaware, our system enables users to receive timely notifications of potential medical conditions before severe symptoms arise, thus improving the effectiveness of electronic health monitoring devices in preventing and managing medical conditions. This advancement contributes to the well-being of individuals and society by enhancing healthcare outcomes and promoting proactive health management.

articleTitle: Sequential Heuristic Model for DDOS Attack Detection in Software-Defined Network
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Software Defined Networking (SDN) is a new networking paradigm that uses a central controller to streamline network administration while increasing flexibility and evolution. Because of its centralized management and programmable nature, SDN is susceptible to distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks which can exploit security weaknesses. These attacks can overload the switch and controller's memory, drain server resources and network bandwidth, disrupting normal user access. This research proposes an anomaly detection technique employing higher-order statistics, such as skewness and kurtosis, to detect DOS and DDoS attacks, specifically focusing on TCP Flood and UDP Flood in an SDN environment. This algorithm efficiently recognizes when an attack occurred and determines the exact moment it occurred. We examined the performance of our algorithm using a dataset transmitted between hosts in an SDN environment, testing it with various window sizes. Through a comparative analysis, we demonstrated the superior capability of our proposed methodology in detecting malicious flows within SDN-based networks. To assess performance, we employed detection rate and FPR (False Positive Rate) as evaluation parameters and validated the effectiveness of our approach utilizing a configuration employed within the Mininet network emulator.

articleTitle: Integrated Guidance and Control System of Launch Vehicle (Zenit-2) Using Backstepping Control with Non-Linear Disturbance Observer for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This study investigates the design, analysis, and simulation of integrated guidance and control of launch vehicles using robust disturbance observer backstepping control for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) applications. Integrated Guidance and Control (IGC) architecture is becoming more popular for launch vehicle technology. Guidance and control loops are merged in IGC to save designing time and improve the accuracy and performance of the launch vehicle. In this research, the IGC is developed for the tracking reference trajectory of Russian launch vehicle Zenit-2 available in literature. During the IGC design, non-linear disturbance observer law is designed and merged into the backstepping controller to manage the impact of the nonlinearity factors. Non-linear disturbance observer bounds the controller to track the reference path robustly. Two controllers are required to fully track the trajectory, i.e., pitch rate backstepping controller and velocity backstepping controller. Each controller is designed with its separate disturbance observer, which caters to disturbances in each parameter. For analysis and verification, two sets of disturbance signals were applied to both controllers. One disturbance signal is a sinusoidal wave, while the other is a combination of a sinusoidal and tangent wave. Results showed that the launch vehicle successfully tracked the reference trajectory under applied disturbances. During this study, MATLAB / SIMULINK is used to design, analyze, and simulate the analytical system. For efficient computing, the ODE solver in MATLAB implements a Runge-Kutta technique with a variable time step with high accuracy. This research is beneficial for a launch vehicle's design and control simulation. It can be used to compute thrust and deflection variation to follow the desired trajectory to obtain a particular orbit under applied disturbances.

articleTitle: Optimized Conditioned Adaptive Barrier Function Integral Terminal SMC for Trajectory Tracking of a Quadcopter System via Quantum PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Quadcopters, as a subset of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), have seen a surge in research interest given their vast application potential in civilian and military arenas. This paper introduces an optimized approach to attitude control in quadcopters. An innovative Conditioned Adaptive Barrier Function Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Controller (CAB FIT-SMC) has been developed to tackle the problem of trajectory tracking in the quadcopter. Moreover, a sliding mode control (SMC) is instituted for comparative analysis. The optimization of these control laws is accomplished using the quantum particle swarm optimization (QPSO) algorithm. This algorithm blends the principles of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and quantum mechanics, offering a metaheuristic approach to optimization. The nonlinear model of the quadcopter has been framed utilizing the Lagrange formalism, integrated with MATLAB's ODE-45, and accounts for gyroscopic moments and aerodynamic effects. The system's asymptotic stability is verified through a Lyapunov stability analysis. The paper includes a comparative analysis of all optimized control laws through graphical and tabular comparative analysis. The efficacy of the control law is evaluated against six performance metrics, namely mean absolute percentage error, root mean square error, integral square error, integral absolute error, integral time absolute error, and integral time square error, to identify the superior control law. A 3D-helical complex trajectory is utilized for evaluating the performance and consistency of the proposed optimized controllers. The results indicate that the CABFIT-SMC controller, optimized with the QPSO algorithm, outperforms the optimized SMC across all performance metrics, thus proving its effectiveness for attitude tracking of a quadcopter system.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Security: Federated Learning with GANs for Effective Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has given rise to security challenges, necessitating the real-time detection and mitigation of cyberattacks. Federated Learning (FL) is promising because it enables collaborative global model training in IoT for attack detection while maintaining data privacy. However, FL-enabled systems for IoT face challenges related to class imbalance, inconsistent data distributions, and increased training time. This paper presents a novel FL-enabled approach for IoT attack detection that effectively resolves class imbalance by utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The proposed approach also handles non-iid data distributions through the implementation of Vertical FL. Additionally, ordinal encoding techniques are employed to enhance detection accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is extensively evaluated on the ToN-IoT and N-BaIoT datasets, the DAEs and MLPs both deep learning (DL) algorithms consistently models achieve high precision, recall, and F1 score on ToN-IoT (MLPs: 99.39%, DAEs: 99.62%) and N-BaIoT datasets (DAEs: 93.66%, MLPs: 94.63 %), demonstrating its capability in improving attack detection accuracy and mitigating the limitations of FL-enabled systems in IoT scenarios.

articleTitle: Software Estimation Process Improvement using Data Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Estimating software development effort holds pivotal significance in the domains of resource allocation, budgeting, and project planning. Despite this importance, achieving precise predictions remains a complex challenge. This study aims to refine software effort assessment precision by investigating the efficacy of a segmentation technique tailored for dataset analysis. This approach involves categorizing interconnected projects into distinct segments based on their size, complexity, and domain characteristics. The inherent assumption is that tasks sharing similar attributes will coalesce within segments. Through such delineation, patterns and trends within each segment can be illuminated. This segmentation technique is anticipated to enhance the accuracy of software effort estimation through meticulous intra-segment effort computations and accounting for variations across segment boundaries. To substantiate this approach, the dataset is partitioned into subsets based on productivity values. Employing machine learning models like Linear, Support Vector Regression (SVR), k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with Exponential Linear Unit (ELU) activation, the study transforms nominal data into numerical form and evaluates model performance using metrics like MMRE, MAE, MdMRE, MdAE, and PRED. The segmentation technique exhibits promising outcomes in elevating software effort estimation accuracy, achieving an average MAE reduction of approximately 6.79 units compared to prior research. This technique holds potential to inform resource allocation and project scheduling decisions in the software industry, advancing estimation processes and empowering more informed strategic choices.

articleTitle: Identification of Potential HUB Genes and Associated Transcription Factors in Rheumatoid Arthritis
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This study aims to inquire the potential hub genes, related pathways and associated transcription factors (TFs) connected with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). It is critical to find hub genes that provide fresh perspectives on the disorder given the autoimmune nature and intricate pathogenesis of RA. To accomplish this, RA gene expression profile from GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) collection was obtained. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were discovered, and enrichment analysis was done to investigate the biological, cellular component and molecular activities of these frequently altered genes. Hub genes were shortlisted by subjecting the protein-protein interaction(PPI) networks to the cytoHubba, plugin of Cytoscape. The Transcriptional Regulatory Relationships Unravelled by Sentence Based Text Mining (TRRUST) database was used to predict TFs. 21,155 DEGs were obtained. Functional enrichment analyses indicated that DEGs were mostly enriched in cytoplasmic translation and the biosynthesis of macromolecules and peptides. These proteins were mostly found in the nucleus, cytoplasmic large ribosomal subunit, focal adhesion, and cell-substrate junctions. In terms of molecular function these proteins participated in RNA, cadherin and purine ribonucleoside triphosphate binding, and regulated protein serine/threonine kinase activity. 13 hub genes were identified, and their associated with top 10 TFs were determined. These 10 TFs were found to regulate five hub genes i.e. EGFR, JUN1, CDH1, STAT1 and HSPA4. This paper offers a critical insight on the important genes and TFs associated with the complex pathology of RA, which could be used as a basis for further experimental study and potential clinical applications.

articleTitle: Inverse Optimal Control Design of a VTOL Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A Vertical Takeoff and Landing (VTOL) aircraft is capable of short/vertical takeoffs and landings, thus eliminating the requirement of long runways. This feature makes them suitable for a broader variety of missions, generally not achievable by a traditional aircraft. The dynamics of the VTOL aircraft in the vertical plane has been used as a benchmark problem to demonstrate the effectiveness of different nonlinear control techniques, mainly due to being highly coupled and non-minimum phase. This paper presents the design of an inverse optimal control for a simplified VTOL aircraft model. The proposed control law is based on a Control Lyapunov Function (CLF) which exploits the normal form typically used for control design through feedback linearization. The suggested control law is compared with dynamic feedback linearization based control law and a comparison is drawn based on their efficacy and robustness.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Framework of Meta-Learning and Generative Adversarial Networks for Few-Shot Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Malware detection poses a significant challenge due to the constant evolution and proliferation of malicious software. Traditional approaches often struggle to keep up with the ever-growing variety of malware samples. In this paper, we offer a hybrid framework (MetaGANet) that combines the power of meta-learning and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to address the problem of few-shot malware detection. By leveraging the capabilities of meta-learning, our framework can rapidly acclimatize to new malware samples with limited training data, thereby enhancing detection performance. The GAN component of our framework generates synthetic malware samples, allowing for robust training and augmenting the available data. We conduct extensive experiments using benchmark dataset miniImagenet and malware dataset Figshare and demonstrate the effectiveness of our hybrid approach. Our results show significant improvements in few-shot malware detection accuracy, surpassing traditional methods. The proposed framework offers a promising solution to the ongoing challenge of efficiently detecting and combating emerging malware threats.

articleTitle: SQUID Sensor Technology: Fundamental Principle and Applications in ASW Operation and Geophysical Exploration
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper describes the basic theory and working principle of Superconducting Quantum Interference Device (SQUID) sensors. These quantum sensors exploit the phenomena of superconductivity leading to flux quantization and Josephson tunneling that measures small variations in the magnetic field down to the range of femtotesla level (~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−15</sup>tesla). SQUIDs are fabricated from superconducting materials and are typically designed to operate using liquid nitrogen (77K) or helium (4.2K). The extreme sensitivity of SQUID sensors makes them ideal for applications and research in a variety of areas such as magnetic anomaly detection - Antisubmarine Warfare (ASW) operation, mine sweeping operation, brain function mapping, etc. From a commercial perspective, SQUIDs are considered the most suitable sensors for application in geophysical exploration because they enable the combination of ultra-high sensitivity and high bandwidth, both of which are crucial for high-quality geophysical surveys. This paper provides also a brief overview of SQUID sensor applications in oceanography, ASW operation, and geophysical exploration.

articleTitle: Spike-Based Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of Blunt Bodies Using Machine Learning and CFD Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Aerodynamic shape optimization of hypersonic vehicles is crucial during the conceptual design stage owing to the formation of powerful bow shockwaves in hypersonic flow. These shockwaves cause high pressures and temperatures at the vehicle's nose leading to a high risk of heat shield failure. The design goals for heat and drag reduction are discovered to be conflicting in the sense that achieving one of them undermines the other. Hence, to counter these risks simultaneously, a forward disk-tip spike can be added as it reduces drag and pressure by forming oblique shocks and separation regions. In this study, various aero-disk configurations of a hypersonic vehicle are investigated at Mach numbers 4.0 to 7.0. Aerodynamic forces and heating characteristics of the blunt bodies with spike-based aerodisk is analyzed at different design conditions using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). After a thorough evaluation of the flow-field characteristics using CFD, machine learning-based prediction of certain geometric and aero-thermodynamic parameters is implemented. This process proves to be an efficient and reliable framework for optimizing and predicting aero-thermodynamic parameters for various fore-body configurations.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Thermal Performance Enhancement of a PCM Heat Sink Under Different Heat Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research focuses on the numerical simulation of heat sinks based on phase change material (PCM) as an efficient cooling solution for portable electronic devices with minimal dissipation. The objective is to tackle the increasing concerns regarding heat management in electronic devices, where excessive heat can lead to malfunctions and failures. PCM-based heat sinks offer benefits including a high latent heat of fusion and cycling stability, but their thermal conductivity value is low which is a cause for concern. This study explores techniques to enhance heat transfer by utilizing thermal conductivity enhancers, comparing the heat sink performance by employing PCM, examines the effect of PCM on temperature reduction time advantages, and temperature uniformity. This research aims to extend the lifespan of electronic devices, improve their performance, and contribute to the ongoing efforts in efficient thermal management strategies.

articleTitle: A Security Analysis of a Blockchain Based Decentralized Energy Trading Application
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The utilization of Blockchain technology for decentralized energy trading is gaining momentum within the energy sector. This technological advancement has facilitated the creation of localized energy markets through the deployment of multiple distributed microgrids. Over recent years, numerous blockchain platforms have been under evaluation for their suitability in these systems. Among these platforms, Bitcoin has undergone comprehensive investigation for its compatibility with such setups. However, due to inherent security and privacy concerns, it has not been chosen as the preferred platform for implementing decentralized energy trading systems. This research paper identifies a security vulnerability within the transaction flow implementation. The paper begins with an overview of a decentralized energy trading system, followed by the formulation of a threat model and its corresponding mathematical framework. Subsequently, the paper presents two scenarios wherein inadequate security measures could be exploited to execute a double spending attack (DSA), aided by a Block Delay Technique.

articleTitle: High-Gain Observer Design for Nonlinear Two-Time-Scale Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In robotics, aerospace, and electromechanical applications, it is common practice to break the dynamics into two timescales for analysis and control design. In modern applications, the observer-based control design has gained much attention to enhance the reliability of closed-loop control. In this article, we have proposed high-gain observer-based output feedback control (OFC) for a class of nonlinear two-time-scale systems that only assumes the knowledge of the output of the system in each timescale and estimates the remaining slow and fast states simultaneously, which was not the case in the existing literature. By the virtue of the separation principle in high-gain observers, the control and observer designs can be carried out separately and then can be implemented simultaneously on the system. The proposed OFC strategy is implemented on a class of nonlinear electromechanical systems. The MATLAB-based numerical simulation results show the efficiency of the proposed high-gain observer in OFC.

articleTitle: Multirotor Aerial Vehicle Attitude Control Using Successive Generalized Dynamic Inversion
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A novel Successive Generalized Dynamic Inversion (SGDI) control strategy is investigated for high-performance autonomous operation of multirotor aerial vehicles. The SGDI framework encompasses two generalized dynamic inversion control loops applied in succession to stabilize the vehicle's attitude and body rate dynamics. The outer loop enforces the prescribed attitude constraint dynamics that fully capture the control objectives, whereas the inner loop is responsible for satisfying the prescribed body rate system-constrained behavior. The constraint dynamics are evaluated along the dynamical system trajectories and are imposed on the closed loop dynamics using dynamically scaled generalized inversion to realize SGDI control in successive manner. Further, a new perspective is introduced by including robust control element within SGDI framework which is pledged to strengthen robustness against system nonlinearities, parametric uncertainties and external perturbations. Detailed stability analysis of SGDI is carried out to guarantee semi-global asymptotically stable attitude and body rate dynamics. Additionally, the tilting pitch and roll commands imperative to minimize the longitudinal and lateral positional errors are generated using classical Proportional Derivative control, which is also accountable for attaining the required altitude. The efficacy and superiority of SGDI control is validated through numerical simulations on six degrees of freedom multirotor simulator of X-4 flyer vehicle developed in Simulink/Matlab under perturbed flight conditions.

articleTitle: Centrifugal Pump Fault Detection with Hybrid Feature Pool and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative hybrid technique for diagnosing faults in centrifugal pumps utilizing vibration sensor data. The initial signal, filtered through a low pass filter with a 4.6 kHz cutoff frequency, undergoes both Stockwell and continuous wavelet transformations concurrently. These transformations yield two sets of time-frequency scalograms as inputs for separate convolutional neural networks. These networks extract vital features from the scalograms, which are then amalgamated into a hybrid feature pool. Because the pool has many dimensions, principal component analysis is used to reduce the feature space to a manageable latent space while keeping the essential features from both sets of scalograms. Subsequently, a two-layer Artificial Neural Network is employed to categorize pump states based on this reduced-dimensional feature space. Impressively, our approach attains a classification accuracy of 95.60%, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. This shows how well our strategy works. It combines different transformation techniques, hybrid feature extraction, and dimensionality reduction to make a method for diagnosing centrifugal pump faults that is very effective and quick.

articleTitle: Cracking the Emotional Code: Identifying Emotions Through Electroencephalograms
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this work, we present a machine-learning model for emotion recognition based on Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. We employed an online available DREAMERs dataset, from which we classify 4 human emotions such as sadness, joy, anger, and pleasure. In the proposed methodology, first, the acquired EEG signals from each subject were divided into smaller non-overlapping segments of 30 secs. Then, we removed the motion artifact and unwanted noise by utilizing a band-stop (48.5–51.5 Hz) infinite impulse response (IIR) filter, after which we extracted 5 frequency bands. The first 4 frequency bands i.e. Delta (1–4 Hz), Theta (4–8 Hz), Alpha (8–12 Hz), and Beta (12–30 Hz) were then fed to band-pass pass IIR filter, whereas the remaining 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> frequency band i.e. Gamma (30 Hz) was provided to a high pass filter to extract a total of 6 time and frequency-based features for each band. Adaptive Synthetic (ADASYN) was used to handle imbalance classes. Moreover, Chi-square (CHI2) algorithm was employed to select the top 50 features out of 420 extracted features. Finally, we utilized various classifiers in order to compare the performance of our model. Fine K- nearest neighbor (KNN) classifier demonstrated the highest accuracy of 91.1% with a training time of approximately 25 secs for emotion detection using EEG signals.

articleTitle: Supervised Classification of Water Bodies: Analyzing Various Methods Through a Case Study of Water Resources in Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, we explore the latest developments in the field of water body classification using satellite imagery, with a particular focus on Pakistani water resources as a case study. The spatial distribution of Earth's water and the change in its dispersion over time has critical implications for agriculture, ecology, and the environment. Classification of water bodies using remote sensing imagery is a significant research domain. Classical machine learning methods such as Random Forest, struggle due to their inability to capture intricate pixel-lovel associations within satellite imagery. However, deep learning and attention-based algorithms have emerged as strong contenders for effectively addressing this limitation. According to our information, no substantial work has been done in Pakistan at the national level aimed at employing Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques for the classification and real-time monitoring of water resources. This study presents a comparative analysis of three techniques: Classical Machine Learning (ML) Algorithms, CNN-based Deep Learning Algorithms, and Attention-based Neural Networks. Leveraging a custom water dataset (PAKSEN2) with Sentinel-2 imagery, the study demonstrates that classical machine learning algorithms underperformed, achieving only 40% accuracy, while a CNN-based ResNet50 network [1] achieved 81%. Remarkably, the attention-based Vision Transformer (ViT) [2] achieved 99% accuracy, outperforming both traditional and CNN-based approaches.

articleTitle: Implementation of Space Exploration Algorithm Duly Integrated with ROS: A Practical Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Exploration is the process of picking target points that contribute the most to a certain gain function in an initially unknown environment. The most popular approach to exploration is frontier-based exploration, in which frontiers are locations on the threshold between open space and undiscovered space. By traveling to a new frontier, the map of the environment is progressively developed, until there are no more new frontiers to detect. For problems involving mobile robot exploration, this study presents meta-heuristic Aquila optimization algorithm with the deterministic method, for comparison and performance testing in mobile robotics. Matlab(R)-Rosintegration tools and real-world tests were carried out in a Gazebo environment utilizing various map scenarios. During the exploration process, the robot updates the sensor visibility frontier line as it travels to unexplored territory. The frontier line's points are taken to be the swarm population, each with its own positions and costs, allowing for the computing of the next way-point (pose) for the robot. The results demonstrated through extensive simulations depicting different environments, duly demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for mobile robotics.

articleTitle: Robust Multi-Object Threat Detection in X-ray Baggage Scanner
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: X-ray Baggage Scanner are deployed at public entry points for threat object detection and classification. Existing surveillance systems cannot function without human assistance. In this paper, we propose a pipe line for automated real time anomaly detection and recognition in X-ray security imagery. However, identifying multiple threat objects in cluttered X-ray images can be a challenging task. For this we have labelled and trained real image from X-ray baggage scanner. Data augmentation is applied to collect synthetic data and is trained and labelled to ensure robustness. The model is fine-tuned using pretrained weights. We achieve 0.85 of mean average precision (mAP) for multi object detection using EfficientDet model. For real world hardware implementation, the model is compressed and transferred to Raspberry pie and Jetson Xavier NX. Comparative analysis with YOLO variants and transformer based models shows that our algorithm outperforms previously proposed methods.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Effect of Rack Arrangement on Energy Consumption in a Data Center using Numerical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In a typical real-world scenario, already available infrastructure is remodeled to be used as a datacenter. As a result, it becomes problematic to follow the industry standard for datacenter design. Subsequently, an increased amount of electricity is required to reach and maintain the optimum server operating temperature. This may be due to inefficient placement of inlets and outlets, a poor server rack arrangement or a combination of both. As a result, the servers might end up over-heating and the datacenter may be required to operate at a reduced capacity. In a worst-case scenario, a powering down of all of the servers might be required until the temperature inside the datacenter falls within the operating range. In this paper, we present an aerothermal “Digital Twin” of the datacenter available at the Digital Pakistan Lab. Furthermore, by using numerical aerothermal simulations we figure out the optimum arrangement of server racks within a pre-existing datacenter, with a goal to reduce electricity consumption. We also design a Computer Room Air Handling (CRAH) system to study the feasibility of its implementation in the datacenter under consideration. We compare rack inlet temperature for various rack arrangements. The results indicate that by changing the rack arrangement to two cold - one hot aisle arrangement as compared to the one cold - one hot aisle arrangement currently implemented, a lower rack inlet temperature can be achieved. Moreover, it is noted that the implementation of the CRAH system will result in further improvement of the overall efficiency of the HVAC system without any major changes to the already existing datacenter infrastructure.

articleTitle: Enhancing Dielectric Strength of Polyester Insulation in Ignition Coils Using Nano and Micro Fillers: A Comparative Study of Al2O3 and ZnO
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This study primarily investigates the challenges related to polyester insulation in ignition coils and explores the potential of utilizing nano and micro fillers, specifically ZnO and A1203, to tackle these issues. The research focuses on examining the dielectric strength of these fillers and observes that with an increase in filler concentration, certain properties are influenced by environmental temperature and humidity variations. Notably, ZnO-filled composites exhibit enhanced interfacial polarization, but a decrease in dielectric strength due to moisture absorption and elevated temperatures. Conversely, Al203-filled specimens demonstrate improved dielectric strength. The estimation of the relationship between relative humidity (RH), temperature, and dielectric strength can be achieved through the utilization of a mathematical model based on the finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: Vehicle Trajectory Estimation in GNSS denied Environments: An analysis of Extended Kalman Filter Approach for Monocular Vision Aided Inertial Navigation
